description: A case in which the Court determined that a federal district court judge has some ability to recall jurors in a civil case after identifying an error in their verdict, subject to certain limitations to ensure the jurors were not prejudiced.

name: Mathis v. United States
description: A case in which the Court determined that a state crime cannot qualify as a predicate offense under the Armed Career Criminal Act (ACCA) if the elements of the state offense are broader than those of a listed generic offense based on an “elements-only inquiry,” not a modified categorical approach.

name: Kirtsaeng v. John Wiley & Sons
description: A case in which the Court determined that, when deciding whether to grant attorney’s fees under Section 505 of the Copyright Act, courts should give substantial weight to the objective reasonableness of the losing party’s position, but that determination should not be the controlling factor.

name: Cuozzo Speed Technologies v. Lee
description: A case in which the Court held that the Patent Trial and Appeal Board may apply the broadest reasonable interpretation of patent claims during an inter partes review proceeding, and such a proceeding is not judicially reviewable.

name: Birchfield v. North Dakota
description: A case in which the Court determined that warrantless blood tests incident to an arrest for drunk driving violate the Fourth Amendment, but warrantless breath tests incident to an arrest for drunk driving do not.

name: Encino Motorcars v. Navarro
description: A case in which the Court held that, because the Department of Labor did not give adequate reasons for altering its position on whether service advisors are exempt from overtime compensation under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA), the case should be remanded for reinterpretation that does not give controlling weight to the Department’s 2011 position.

name: Universal Health Services, Inc. v. Escobar
description: A case in which the Court held that the implied certification test could be a valid basis for False Claims Act liability, and the conditions of payment with which the defendant allegedly failed to comply did not need to be explicitly stated.

name: United States v. Bryant
description: A case in which the Court determined that the use of an uncounseled conviction in tribal court proceedings that complied with the Indian Civil Rights Act of 1968 (ICRA) as a predicate offense under 18 U.S.C. 117(a) did not violate the Sixth Amendment.

name: United States v. Texas
description: A case in which the equally divided Court affirmed the lower court's judgment that the Deferred Action for Parents of Americans and Lawful Permanent Residents (DAPA) program was arbitrary and capricious, and failed to undergo notice-and-comment procedures as required by the Administrative Procedure Act.

name: United States Army Corps of Engineers v. Hawkes Co., Inc.
description: A case in which the Court determined that the Army Corps of Engineers’ jurisdictional determination that a property constituted “water of the United States” was a final agency action subject to judicial review under the Administrative Procedure Act.

name: Welch v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that the rule the Supreme Court announced in Johnson v. United States regarding what constitutes a violent offense for the purposes of sentencing under the Armed Career Criminal Act applies retroactively.

name: Sheriff v. Gillie
description: A case in which the Court held that, regardless of whether special counsel appointed by the Attorney General to collect debts are “state officers” under the Federal Debt Collection Practices Act, the use of Attorney General letterhead by such special counsel is not materially misleading.

name: Ross v. Blake
description: A case in which the Court determined that the Prison Litigation Reform Act’s requirement to exhaust administrative remedies does not have a “special circumstances” exception.

name: Betterman v. Montana
description: A case in which the Court determined that the Sixth Amendment’s guarantee of a speedy trial does not extend past a guilty verdict or guilty plea.

name: CRST Van Expedited v. EEOC
description: A case in which the Court determined that a defendant may be a “prevailing party” for the purpose of the award of fees even without a ruling on the merits.

name: Zubik v. Burwell
description: A case in which the Court determined that insurance companies could potentially provide contraceptive coverage to employees of organizations that object to such coverage on religious grounds without the organizations needing to provide notification.

name: Simmons v. Himmelreich
description: A case in which the Court determined that the judgment bar of the Federal Tort Claims Act (FTCA) does not apply to claims dismissed for falling under the exceptions to the FTCA.

name: Puerto Rico v. Franklin California Tax-Free Trust
description: A case in which the Court determined that Chapter 9 of the Bankruptcy Code preempted the Puerto Rico statute that allowed public utilities to restructure their debt.

name: Wittman v. Personhuballah
description: A case in which the Court determined that members of Congress whose chances of reelection might be impaired by a new districting plan did not have standing under Article III of the U.S. Constitution to appeal their case to the Supreme Court.

name: RJR Nabisco v. The European Community
description: A case in which the Court held that some sections of the Racketeer Influenced Corrupt Organizations (RICO) statute can apply extraterritorially because Congress clearly based them on predicate offenses that can occur outside of the United States.

name: Whole Woman’s Health v. Hellerstedt
description: A case in which the Court determined that the regulations at issue unconstitutionally imposed an undue burden on women seeking abortions because they created a substantial burden and did not actually serve the stated government interest.

name: Nichols v. United States
description: A case in which the Court determined that the Sexual Offender Registration and Notification Act does not require a sex offender who is moving to a country outside of U.S. jurisdiction to update his residence with the sexual offender registry.

name: Husky Electronics v. Ritz
description: A case in which the Court determined that the “actual fraud” language of the bankruptcy statute encompasses traditional forms of fraud and is not limited to fraudulent representation.

name: Williams v. Pennsylvania
description: A case in which the Court determined that the Eighth and Fourteenth Amendments are violated when a judge who was previously involved in the case as a prosecutor declines to recuse himself, regardless of whether that judge’s decision as part of a multi-member tribunal was dispositive.

name: Voisine v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that a reckless domestic violence assault qualifies as misdemeanor crime of domestic violence for the purpose of prohibiting firearm possession.

name: Hughes v. Talen Energy Marketing, LLC
description: A case in which the Court determined that the Federal Power Act preempted state regulation of utility contracts and sales.

name: Taylor v. United States
description: A case in which the Court determined that, in a prosecution for robbery under the Hobbs Act, the commerce element is satisfied when the government shows that the defendant robbed a drug dealer of drugs or drug proceeds.

name: Halo Electronics v. Pulse Electronics Inc.
description: A case in which the Court determined that the rigid two-part test is not necessary for determining whether a patentee is eligible for enhanced damages under 35 U.S.C §284.

name: Kingdomware Technologies, Inc. v. United States
description: A case in which the Court determined that the Court had jurisdiction to address the merits of the case even if the contracts had already been performed, and the Department of Veterans Affairs’ “set-aside” for veteran-owned businesses is mandatory.

name: Utah v. Strieff
description: A case in which the Court determined that, in the absence of flagrant police misconduct, the discovery of a valid, pre-existing, and untainted arrest warrant attenuated the connection between the unconstitutional investigatory stop and the evidence seized incident to the lawful arrest.

name: Nebraska v. Parker
description: A case in which the Court determined that the passage of the 1882 Act by Congress did not diminish the original boundaries of the Omaha Indian Reservation.

name: Sturgeon v. Frost
description: A case in which the Court held that the Alaska National Interest Lands Conservation Act of 1980 did not allow the National Park Service to regulate all land physically within the boundaries of the National Park System in Alaska.

name: Americold Realty Trust v. Conagra Foods, Inc., et al.
description: A case in which the Court determined that, for the purposes of diversity jurisdiction, the citizenship of a trust is based on the citizenship of its members, which includes the beneficiary shareholders as well as the trustees.

name: Heffernan v. City of Paterson
description: A case in which the Court determined that a government employee who is demoted because of perceived involvement in protected political activity is entitled to challenge his demotion under the First Amendment, even if the demotion was based on a factual mistake.

name: Bank Markazi v. Peterson
description: A case in which the Court decided that a statute effectively directing a particular result in a single pending case does not violate the separation of powers.

name: Puerto Rico v. Sanchez Valle
description: A case in which the Court held that Puerto Rico and the U.S. federal government are the same sovereign entity for the purpose of the Double Jeopardy Clause.

name: Molina-Martinez v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that an error in the application of the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines that results in the wrong Guideline range affected the defendant’s substantial rights.

name: Duncan v. Owens
description: A case in which the Court will determine whether habeas relief can be awarded in the absence of clearly established precedent that the inference of motive at trial violates the defendant’s right to due process.

name: Friedrichs v. California Teachers Association
description: A case in which the Court will determine whether the California agency shop arrangements and opt-out requirements for union relationships violate the First Amendment.

name: Fisher v. University of Texas
description: A case in which the Court determined that the University of Texas’ use of race as a consideration in the admissions process did not violate the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.

name: Evenwel v. Abbott
description: A case in which the Court determined that the “one person, one vote” principle of the Equal Protection Clause allows a state to draw its legislative districts based on total population.

name: Harris v. Arizona Independent Redistricting Commission
description: A case in which the Court determined that the creation of voting districts that deviate from the “one person, one vote” principle may be justified by legitimate considerations, such as a desire to comply with the Voting Rights Act as it was in effect at the time of the plan.

name: Dollar General Corporation v. Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians
description: A case in which the equally divided Court affirmed the lower court, determining a tribal court had jurisdiction to adjudicate civil tort claims against nonmembers.

name: Franchise Tax Board of California v. Hyatt
description: A case in which the Court determined that the Constitution does not allow Nevada to refuse to extend to other states haled into Nevada courts the same immunities Nevada would receive in those courts.

name: Gobeille v. Liberty Mutual Insurance Co.
description: A case in which the Court determined that the reporting requirements of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA) preempt a Vermont state statute regarding reporting requirements as applied to a self-insured employee health plan.

name: Menominee Indian Tribe of Wisconsin v. United States
description: A case in which the Court determined that there were no extraordinary circumstances out of the Menominee Indian Tribe’s control to toll the statute of limitations from running.

name: Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Smith, Inc. v. Manning
description: A case in which the Court determined that the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 creates the same test for establishing federal jurisdiction as the general test for whether a federal court has jurisdiction: Whether the case “arises under” federal law.

name: Green v. Brennan
description: A case in which the Court held that the 45-day period in which an employee must file a constructive discharge claim under federal employment discrimination law begins to run on the date the employee resigns.

name: Musacchio v. United States
description: A case in which the Court determined that the law of the case doctrine does not require that the sufficiency of evidence be measured against the elements laid out in the jury instructions when those elements require the government to prove more than the statute requires and the government did not object at trial. The Court also determined that a statute of limitations defense that is not raised at trial is not reviewable on appeal.

name: Luis v. United States
description: A case in which the Court determined that the pretrial restraining of a defendant's assets untainted by their crime that are needed to retain counsel of choice violates the Sixth Amendment.

name: Tyson Foods, Inc. v. Bouaphakeo
description: A case in which the Court determined that a class action is properly certified and maintained, despite differences among the plaintiff class, if all the individual plaintiffs' cases ask the same central question and even if some plaintiffs were not injured and have no legal right to damages.

name: Montanile v. Board of Trustees of the National Elevator Industrial Health Benefit Plan
description: A case in which the Court determined that the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 does not allow for a suit to recover reimbursement of an asset that has been fully disbursed on non-traceable items such as services.

name: Shapiro v. McManus
description: A case in which the Court held that a claim covered by the Three-Judge Court Act must be heard by a three-judge panel.

name: Bruce v. Samuels
description: A case in which the Court will determine whether the Prison Litigation Reform Act caps the monthly payment to cover a prisoner’s filing fees at 20% of the prisoner’s monthly income regardless of the number of pending cases the prisoner has in federal courts.

name: Lockhart v. United States
description: A case in which the Court determined that a prior conviction of “aggravated sexual abuse” or “sexual abuse” may trigger a mandatory minimum sentence, even when the prior conviction did not involve a minor.

name: Luna Torres v. Lynch
description: A case in which the Court determined that a state offense may constitute an aggravated felony for the purpose of the removal of a permanent resident when it includes all the elements of the federal statute with the exception of the interstate commerce element.

name: Spokeo, Inc. v. Robins
description: A case in which the Court held that lower courts need to consider the elements of Article III standing analysis separately in determining whether standing is sufficient for a federal court to hear the case.

name: Foster v. Chatman
description: A case in which the Court determined that the new evidence in this case was sufficient to establish that there was purposeful discrimination of the type that Batson v. Kentucky prohibits in the jury selection process of Foster’s trial.

name: Campbell-Ewald Company v. Gomez
description: A case in which the Court held that an unaccepted settlement offer does not make a plaintiff’s claim moot, and a federal contractor does not have derivative sovereign liability from a suit under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act.

name: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission v. Electric Power Supply Association, et al.
description: A case in which the Court held that the Federal Power Act (FPA) grants the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) the authority to regulate wholesale market operators’ compensation for reduction in electricity consumption, and the rule in question was not arbitrary and capricious.

name: Hurst v. Florida
description: A case in which the Court held that Florida’s sentencing scheme violated the Sixth Amendment’s guarantee of a jury trial in light of the Supreme Court’s decision in Ring v. Arizona, which held that the Sixth Amendment required a jury to sentence the defendant to death.

name: Montgomery v. Louisiana
description: A case in which the Court held that the Supreme Court’s decision in Miller v. Alabama, which prohibits sentencing schemes that impose a punishment of mandatory life without parole for juvenile offenders convicted of homicide, applied retroactively.

name: Kansas v. Carr
description: A case in which the Court decided that the Eighth Amendment does not require that a jury be instructed that mitigating circumstances do not need to be proven beyond a reasonable doubt, nor does it require that the sentencing phase of a joint trial be severed.

name: DIRECTV, Inc. v. Imburgia
description: A case in which the Court determined that the Federal Arbitration Act preempted state law and required the enforcement of a contract’s arbitration agreement.

name: Ocasio v. United States
description: A case in which the Court determined that a conspiracy to commit extortion can involve the purported victims of the extortion as members of the conspiracy.

name: OBB Personenverkehr AG v. Sachs
description: A case in which the Court held that the commercial activity exception to the Foreign Sovereign Immunity Act only applies when the suit is based upon activity that took place in the United States, and it was not sufficient to establish a single element of the claim in question.

name: Hawkins v. Community Bank of Raymore
description: A case in which an equally-divided Court affirmed the lower court in that spousal guarantors could not be considered “applicants” for the purposes of the protections the Equal Credit Opportunity Act provides.

name: Reyes Mata v. Lynch
description: A case in which the Court held that circuit courts of appeals have jurisdiction over Board of Immigration Appeals decisions to deny motions to reopen immigration proceedings.

name: Glossip v. Gross
description: A case in which the Court held that the use of midazolam as the initial drug in a state’s execution protocol does not violate the Eighth Amendment’s prohibition against cruel and unusual punishment.

name: Obergefell v. Hodges
description: A case in which the Court held that the Fourteenth Amendment requires states to license and recognize same-sex marriage.

name: Kingsley v. Hendrickson
description: A case in which the Court held that a pretrial detainee who brings an excessive force claim need only prove that the use of force in question was objectively unreasonable.

name: Horne v. Department of Agriculture
description: A case in which the Court determined that the reserve requirement of the Department of Agriculture’s Marketing Order constituted a per se taking and therefore required that the government provide just compensation.

name: McFadden v. United States
description: A case in which the Court decided that in order to fulfill the intent element of The Controlled Substance Analogue Enforcement Act of 1986, a person must either know that the substance is a controlled substance or be aware of what the substance is without knowing that it is controlled.

name: Bullard v. Blue Hills Bank, fka Hyde Park Savings
description: A case in which the Court held that a bankruptcy court’s order denying confirmation of a repayment plan is not a final order for the purpose of immediate appeal.

name: Harris v. Viegelahn
description: A case in which the Court held that any assets acquired after the date of filing for Chapter 13 bankruptcy must be returned to the debtor when the bankruptcy is converted to Chapter 7.

name: Kimble v. Marvel
description: A case in which the Court determined that its earlier decision in Brulotte v. Thys Co., which held that a patentee cannot continue to receive royalties after the expiration of the patent, should be upheld.

name: Commil USA, LLC v. Cisco Systems, Inc.
description: A case in which the Court decided that a good-faith belief that a patent is invalid is not a defense to a claim of induced infringement.

name: Brumfield v. Cain
description: A case in which the Court held that a state court’s decision that a defendant was not entitled to an evidentiary hearing on intellectual disability despite evidence of a borderline IQ score and potential adaptive skills impairment was an unreasonable determination of facts.

name: Michigan v. Environmental Protection Agency
description: A case in which the Court determined that the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) unreasonably interpreted the Clean Air Act by not considering costs to power plants in deciding that regulation was “appropriate and necessary.”

name: Bank of America v. Caulkett
description: A case in which the court ruled that Section 506 (d) of the Bankruptcy Code does not allow a debtor filing for bankruptcy to void a second mortgage when the debt owed on the first one exceeds the value of the collateral property.

name: City and County of San Francisco v. Sheehan
description: A case in which the Court held that an unwarranted entry does not violate the Fourth Amendment when it does not violate a clearly established constitutional or statutory right and is reasonable under the circumstances.

name: Walker v. Texas Division, Sons of Confederate Veterans, Inc.
description: Texas' specialty license plates constitute government speech that does not require viewpoint neutrality under the First Amendment.

name: King v. Burwell
description: A case in which the Court determined that the plain language of the Affordable Care Act extended tax credits to federally-created exchanges as well as those the states created.

name: City of Los Angeles v. Patel
description: A case in which the Court determined that a municipal ordinance that allows the police to inspect hotel records without a warrant violates the Fourth Amendment’s prohibition against unreasonable searches unless the business owner is given the opportunity for pre-compliance review.

name: Davis v. Ayala
description: A case in which the Court held that, when a state court has adjudicated constitutional claims on the merits, a federal court can only overturn that determination if the state court’s decision was based on an unreasonable view of the facts or contrary to clearly established federal law, and that there must be grave doubt regarding whether a possible constitutional error was harmless in order to hold that it was not.

name: Arizona State Legislature v. Arizona Independent Redistricting Commission
description: A case in which the Court determined that the Elections Clause of the U.S. Constitution does not prohibit a state from creating an independent redistricting commission by initiative.

name: Ohio v. Clark
description: A case in which the Court held that the introduction of a child’s testimony at trial through a teacher does not violate the Confrontation Clause of the Sixth Amendment.

name: Baker Botts, LLP v. ASARCO, LLC
description: A case in which the Court held that the Bankruptcy Code does not provide an explicit statutory exception to the American rule of attorney fees—that each litigant pays for his own attorney’s fees.

name: Equal Employment Opportunity Commission v. Abercrombie & Fitch Stores, Inc.
description: A case in which the Court held that an employer may be held liable under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act if an applicant can show that her need for an accommodation was a motivating factor in the employer’s decision not to hire her.

name: Henderson v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that a felony conviction does not prevent a court from ordering the transfer of lawfully owned firearms to a third party as long as the defendant will neither use them nor direct their use.

name: Tibble v. Edison International
description: A case in which the Court held that, according to trust law, the fiduciary duty includes a continuing duty to monitor investments, and that a breach of that duty within six years of the filing of a lawsuit under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act is sufficient to allow the case to proceed.

name: Coleman v. Tollefson
description: A case in which the Court held that a district court’s dismissal of a lawsuit counts as a “strike” for the purpose of the Prison Litigation Reform Act’s “three strikes” provision when the case is pending on appeal.

name: Kerry v. Din
description: A case in which the Court held that the lack of a detailed explanation for a denial of a visa application does not violate the Due Process Clause of the Fifth Amendment.

name: Texas Dept. of Housing and Community Affairs v. Inclusive Communities Project, Inc.
description: A case in which the Court determined that evidence of disparate impact is sufficient to allege a claim that the defendant violated the Fair Housing Act.

name: Rodriguez v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that the use of a K-9 unit at the conclusion of an otherwise lawful traffic stop constituted an unreasonable search and seizure in violation of the Fourth Amendment.

name: Williams-Yulee v. The Florida Bar
description: A case in which the Court held that a rule prohibiting judicial candidates from personally soliciting campaign funds does not violate the First Amendment.

name: Armstrong v. Exceptional Child Center, Inc.
description: A case that determines whether or not a private right of action exists under the Medicaid Act.

name: Mellouli v. Lynch
description: The Government must prove the connection between a state drug paraphernalia conviction and a substance listed in the Controlled Substances Act to trigger deportability under the Immigration and Nationality Act.

name: Wellness International Network v. Sharif
description: A case in which the Court held that claims that would normally be adjudicated by an Article III court can be adjudicated in a non-Article III court as long as the parties knowingly and voluntarily consent.

name: Kellogg Brown & Root v. U.S. ex rel. Carter
description: The Wartime Suspension of Limitations Act's statute of limitations tolling provision does not apply to claims of civil fraud brought by private parties. The False Claims Act's "first-to-file bar" keeps new claims out of court only while related claims are still alive, but not in perpetuity.

name: Mach Mining, LLC v. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission
description: A case in which the Court held that judicial review of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission’s efforts at conciliation is appropriate, but such review must be limited to the narrow requirements that Title VII imposes.

name: Oneok, Inc. et al. v. Learjet, Inc. et al.
description: A case in which the Court held that the Natural Gas Act does not pre-empt state law claims brought by litigants who purchased gas in retail transactions.

name: Reed et al. v. Town of Gilbert, Arizona et al.
description: A case in which the Court decided that extra restrictions placed on signs describing the location of nonprofit events do not survive strict scrutiny and are therefore unconstitutional.

name: United States v. Kwai Fun Wong
description: A case in which the Court held that the statutes of limitations provisions of the Federal Tort Claims Act are subject to equitable tolling.

name: Gelboim v. Bank of America
description: A case in which the Court ruled that a dismissed claim is immediately appealable if the claim is part of a consolidated action and no final order has been issued concerning all claims in the action.

name: Alabama Department of Revenue v. CSX Transportation, Inc.
description: A case in which the Court held that, in evaluating whether a tax is discriminatory under the Railroad Revitalization and Regulatory Reform Act of 1974, courts may consider competitors an appropriate comparison class and must examine the tax code as a whole rather than solely the challenged provision.

name: Direct Marketing Association v. Brohl
description: A case in which the Court held that the Tax Injunction Act does not prevent federal court review of state tax laws, unless such review could restrict the ability of the state to assess or collect its own taxes.

name: U.S. Department of Transportation v. Association of American Railroads
description: A case in which the Court held that for purposes of the validity of metrics and standards, Amtrak is a governmental entity.

name: Young v. United Parcel Service, Inc.
description: A case in which the Court held that the Pregnancy Discrimination Act requires courts to consider whether an employer’s policies treat pregnant workers less favorably than non-pregnant workers with similar inabilities to work and whether there are legitimate reasons for such differences.

name: Hana Financial, Inc. v. Hana Bank
description: A case in which the Court held that "trademark tacking" is a mixed question of fact and law to be decided by the jury.

name: B&B Hardware Inc. v. Hargis Industries Inc.
description: A case in which the Court held that a decision on an issue by an administrative agency can preclude re-litigation of that issue in federal court.

name: Whitfield v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that forced accompaniment during the commission of a crime occurs when a person requires another to “go with” him, even when that movement occurs over a short distance.

name: Perez v. Mortgage Bankers Association
description: A case in which the Court ruled that federal agencies do not need to engage in a notice-and-comment procedure before significantly altering an interpretation of a rule of agency regulation.

name: Elonis v. United States
description: A case in which the Court found that in order to violate the transmission of threats provision, the threat requires both an objective and subjective intent.

name: Comptroller of the Treasury of Maryland v. Wynne
description: A case in which the Court held that the dormant Commerce Clause prohibits the operation of Maryland’s tax scheme because it discriminates against interstate commerce.

name: Alabama Legislative Black Caucus v. Alabama
description: A case in which the Court held that states may not substitute their own extraneous goals for the traditional goals of the Voting Rights Act of 1965 when redrawing electoral districts.

name: M&G Polymers USA, LLC v. Tackett
description: A case in which the Court ruled that collective bargaining agreements should always be interpreted according to ordinary principles of contract law.

name: T-Mobile South, LLC v. City of Roswell, Georgia
description: A case in which the Court held that the Telecommunications Act of 1996 does not require localities to provide reasons for their denial of construction applications in the written denial notification as long as the reasons appear in some other sufficiently clear written record.

name: Johnson v. United States
description: A case in which the Court determined that the residual clause of the Armed Criminal Career Act is unconstitutionally vague.

name: Yates v. United States
description: A case in which the Court ruled that a “tangible item” as defined by Section 1519 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act is one used to record or preserve information.

name: Jesinoski v. Countrywide Home Loans, Inc.
description: A case in which the Court ruled that the Truth in Lending Act allows a borrower to rescind a loan by notifying the creditor within the three-year time frame, even though a lawsuit has not yet been filed.

name: Department of Homeland Security v. MacLean
description: A case in which the Court ruled that the Whistleblower Protection Act bars an agency from taking enforcement action against employees who intentionally disclose sensitive security information.

name: Omnicare, Inc. v. Laborers District Council Construction Industry Pension Fund
description: A case in which the Court ruled that a statement of opinion, even if shown to be objectively false, cannot constitute an untrue statement of fact because of the different nature between opinions and facts.

name: Zivotofsky v. Kerry
description: A case in which the Court held that a federal statute directing the Secretary of State to record the birthplace of a citizen born in Jerusalem as “Israel” if requested to do so impermissibly infringed on the President’s power to recognize foreign states.

name: Jennings v. Stephens
description: A case in which the Court held that a federal habeas petitioner who prevailed in district court does not need to file a separate certificate of appealability to respond to the state's appeal.

name: Teva Pharmaceuticals USA, Inc. v. Sandoz, Inc.
description: A case in which the Court ruled that a federal appellate court can only overturn a district court’s finding of fact if those findings were determined to be “clearly erroneous.”

name: Kansas v. Nebraska and Colorado
description: A case in which the Court ruled that Nebraska violated a compact apportioning the water resources of the Republican River among Kansas, Nebraska and Colorado.

name: North Carolina Board of Dental Examiners v. Federal Trade Commission
description: A case in which the Court ruled that when a state agency is operated by market participants who are elected by other market participants, the agency is a private actor and subject to federal antitrust laws.

name: Integrity Staffing Solutions, Inc. v. Busk
description: A case in which the Court ruled that employees of Integrity Staffing Solutions, Inc. could not be compensated for time spent passing through security checkpoints, because the checkpoints were not integral to their principal duties as employees.

name: Warger v. Shauers
description: A case in which the Court held that the Federal Rule of Evidence 606(b) bars the testimony of a juror regarding statements made during deliberations for the purpose of showing alleged dishonesty by a prospective juror during jury selection.

name: Holt v. Hobbs
description: A case in which the Court held that the Department of Corrections' grooming policy violated an inmate's right to religious exercise.

name: Dart Cherokee Basin Operating Company LLC v. Owens
description: A case in which the Court ruled that a defendant seeking removal of a case to federal court is not required to provide evidence supporting federal jurisdiction in the notice of removal.

name: Heien v. North Carolina
description: A case in which the Court decided that search and seizures are acceptable if a police officer made a reasonable factual or legal mistake.

name: Limelight Networks v. Akamai Technologies
description: A case in which the Court held that a party is not liable for patent infringement under 35 U.S.C. § 271(b) unless the party has also violated Section 217(a)o or any other statutory provision.

name: Riley v. California
description: A case in which the Court found that the San Diego Police Department's search of an arrested gang member's cell phone pictures without a warrant violated the Fourth Amendment.

name: Lane v. Franks
description: A case in which the Court held that a public employee's truthful testimony under subpoena in a trial is citizen speech and thus cannot be used to terminate the employee.

name: Nautilus, Inc. v. Biosig Instruments, Inc.
description: A case in which the Court held that, although a U.S. patent may be vague in certain areas, it is still protected by patent law as long as the patent is definite enough for the general public to know what has or has not been patented already.

name: United States v. Clarke
description: A case in which the Court held that an allegation of improper purpose was not sufficient to entitle a taxpayer to examine IRS officials.

name: CTS Corp. v. Waldburger
description: A case in which the Court found that the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act pre-empts statutes of limitations, but cannot be used to pre-empt statutes of repose.

name: Susan B. Anthony List v. Driehaus
description: A case in which the Court held that pre-enforcement challenges are justiciable when evidence indicates that threatened enforcement of the law is sufficiently imminent.

name: ABC, Inc. v. Aereo, Inc.
description: A case in which the Court held that Aereo, Inc. violated federal copyright law by allowing users to stream content produced by major cable companies without a cable subscription.

name: Pom Wonderful, LLC v. The Coca-Cola Company
description: A case in which the Court held that it is the duty of the court system to harmonize statutes, and that barring one applicable statute by use of another represents a disregard of the law's intent of having cooperative statutes.

name: Argentina v. NML Capital, Ltd.
description: A case in which the Court held that, under the Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act, property held within the US by foreign nations cannot be attached to civil claims unless certain exceptions are met.

name: Fifth Third Bancorp v. Dudenhoeffer
description: A case in which the Court held that a trustee of an employee stock ownership plan is subject to the same duty of prudence as the trustee of a Employee Retirement Income Security Act.

name: Loughrin v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that, to find someone guilty of bank fraud, only one of the two bank fraud statutes must be met, not both.

name: Alice Corporation v. CLS Bank International
description: A case in which the Court found that patent laws should not place restraints on abstract ideas that form the "building blocks of human ingenuity."

name: Wood v. Moss
description: A case in which the Court held that Secret Service agents did not break any "clearly established" laws in their efforts to protect the President, and were thus protected by qualified immunity.

name: Burwell v. Hobby Lobby Stores
description: A case in which the Court decided that the Affordable Care Act's requirement of for-profit corporations to supply its employees with contraceptives that go against the owners' beliefs is unconstitutional under the Religious Freedom Restoration Act of 1993.

name: Clark v. Rameker
description: A case in which the Court held that the U.S. Bankruptcy Code does not exempt inherited retirement accounts from a debtor's estate in bankruptcy proceedings.

name: Halliburton Co. v. Erica P. John Fund, Inc.
description: A case in which the Court held that there is no undue burden in allowing defendants in securities fraud cases from presenting evidence regarding the alleged impact of the misinformation on stock prices.

name: Plumhoff v. Rickard
description: A case in which the Court held that police using deadly force to prevent a crime endangering the general public are granted qualified immunity.

name: Hall v. Florida
description: A case in which the Court held that the execution of intellectually disabled individuals violated the protection against cruel and unusual punishment guaranteed in the Eighth Amendment.

name: Octane Fitness v. ICON Health & Fitness
description: A case in which the Court defined "exceptional" cases as ones that simply stand out from others due to a frivolous nature related to its legal claims.

name: Highmark v. Allcare Management Systems
description: A case in which the Court held that a district court is the best place to determine whether or not a lawsuit is objectively baseless.

name: Robers v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that, under the Mandatory Victims Restitution Act, individuals accused of property crime must pay “an amount equal to...the value of the property,” minus “the value...of any part of the property that is returned" in retribution.

name: Utility Air Regulatory Group v. EPA
description: A case in which the Court held that, under the Clean Air Act, the EPA is not required to include greenhouse gas emissions every time it mentions air pollution.

name: Abramski v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that a firearm purchaser's intent to sell their gun to another buyer is necessary information for the seller's records.

name: Paroline v. United States
description: A case in which the Court ruled that to recover restitution, either the government or the victim must establish a causal relationship between the defendant's conduct and the victim's harm or damages.

name: Prado Navarette v. California
description: A case in which the Court ruled that the Fourth Amendment does not require an officer who received information regarding drunken or reckless driving to independently corroborate the behavior before stopping the vehicle.

name: Harris v. Quinn
description: A case in which the Court held that the the First Amendment prohibits the collection of union dues from home health care providers who do not wish to join a union.

name: Petrella v. MGM, Inc.
description: A case in which the Court held that the doctrine of laches could not be used to prevent a copyright suit that seeks relief for damages that occurred within the three-year window allowed by the Copyright Act.

name: McCullen v. Coakley
description: A case in which the Court ruled that the Massachusetts legislature violated the freedom of speech protections of the First Amendment when it created a 35-foot buffer around the entrances, exits and driveways of abortion clinics where political activity was prohibited.

name: United States v. Castleman
description: A case in which the Court held that a Tennessee man's conviction of domestic violence under state law also prevented him from legally possessing firearms under federal law.

name: United States v. Quality Stores
description: A case in which the Court found that severance payments made to employees who were unwillingly laid off are taxable under the Federal Insurance Contributions Act.

name: Executive Benefits Insurance Agency v. Arkison
description: A case in which the Court found that a bankruptcy judge may hear arguments and file a report with a district court for "non-core" bankruptcy issues.

name: Brandt Revocable Trust v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that the General Railroad Right-of-Way Act of 1875 guaranteed the federal government easements for federally-granted railroad land, but not an enduring property interest.

name: National Labor Relations Board v. Noel Canning
description: A case in which the Court further defined the limitations on the presidential powers granted by the Recess Appointments Clause.

name: Law v. Siegel
description: A case in which the Court found that a bankruptcy court may not enforce specific statutory exceptions.

name: White v. Woodall
description: A case in which the Court held that a guilty plea negates a person's rights against self-incrimination in court.

name: Lozano v. Montoya Alvarez
description: A case in which the Court held that the policy of equitable tolling does not apply to the statute of limitations outlined in the Hauge Convention's provision on international child abduction.

name: Environmental Protection Agency v. EME Homer City Generation
description: A case in which the Court held that the EPA has an absolute mandate to require states to meet federal standards set forth in the Clean Air Act.

name: Scialabba v. Cuellar De Osorio
description: A case in which the Court held that the Immigration and Nationality Act does not allow children who have submitted an application for a visa to keep their original application date if they "aged out" before it was processed.

name: Air Wisconsin Airlines Corp. v. Hoeper
description: A case in which the Court ruled that the Aviation and Transportation Security Act protects transportation officials from false statements, as long as the statements are not materially false within the ATSA context.

name: Ray Haluch Gravel Co. v. Central Pension Fund
description: A case in which the Court held that a district court's decision on a case based on merit is a "final answer" in terms of an eventual appeal.

name: United States v. Apel
description: A case in which the Court ruled that a federal statute can be enforced on a portion of military land that is subject to a public roadway easement.

name: Lexmark International v. Static Control Components
description: A case in which the Court held that the Lanham Act allowed any party to sue for injuries relating to false advertising, as long as the party bringing suit has an interest that falls in the zone of interest that is protected by law.

name: Northwest, Inc. v. Ginsberg
description: A case in which the Court held that the Airline Deregulation Act preempts claims arising from a frequent flier complaint based on price, route, or air carrier service.

name: Michigan v. Bay Mills Indian Community
description: A case in which the Court held that Indian tribes have sovereign immunity that can only be revoked by Congress, and that the immunity extends to their commercial activities, even if they are not on their protected land.

name: BG Group PLC v. Argentina
description: A case in which the Court held that it is the duty of the arbitrating party in a contract lawsuit to interpret provisions outlined in the contract.

name: Fernandez v. California
description: A case in which the Court decided a warrantless search is lawful if one of two co-tenants consents to the search and the other tenant is not present.

name: Unite Here Local 355 v. Mulhall
description: A case which the Court dismissed regarding the Labor Management Relations Act and a company's deals with union members.

name: Rosemond v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that the state must prove that an individual intended to commit or assist in committing a firearm-related offense in a drug trafficking case to be charged with offenses related to the firearm.

name: Lawson and Zang v. FMR, LLC
description: A case in which the Court held that the whistleblower-protection section of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act applies to privately-employed individuals.

name: Burrage v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that, under 21 U.S.C. § 841(b) of the statute regarding drug-related deaths, an individual convicted of the death of another through the sale of drugs cannot be convicted of drug-induced homicide if multiple drugs are present in the deceased's system.

name: Mississippi, ex rel. Hood v. AU Optronics Corp.
description: A case in which the Court ruled that, in order for a case to be removed to a federal district court instead of a state court under the Class Action Fairness Act, at least 100 people must be represented by the lawsuit.

name: Town of Greece v. Galloway
description: A case in which the Court ruled that the invocation of prayer at a legislative session does not violate the Establishment Clause of the First Amendment.

name: Sprint Communications Co. v. Jacobs
description: A case in which the Court held that a federal court does not need to abstain from deciding a case only because there is a case in state court that deals with the same subject matter.

name: Medtronic, Inc. v. Boston Scientific Corp.
description: A case in which the Court held that, in a patent infringement case, the burden of proof of infringement is on the patent holder.

name: Bond v. United States
description: A case in which the Court found that international treaties cannot overstep state sovereignty, and enforcement should be limited to international affairs.

name: Walden v. Fiore
description: A case in which the Court held that an FDA officer could not be sued in Nevada under the Fourteenth Amendment, due to his lack of connection with that state.

name: Sandifer v. United States Steel Corporation
description: A case in which the Court held that putting on safety garments constitutes "changing clothes" under the Fair Labor Standards Act.

name: Kansas v. Cheever
description: A case in which the Court held that, in a criminal trial, the Fifth Amendment allows a prosecutor to use psychiatric evidence to counter-argue psychiatric evidence given by the defense.

name: Kaley v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that the Fifth and Sixth Amendments do not allow an individual to use funds obtained illegally to pay for an attorney.

name: Schuette v. Coalition to Defend Affirmative Action
description: A case in which the Court held that the judiciary did not have standing to overturn the state constitutional amendment regarding affirmative action in school admissions.

name: Daimler AG v. Bauman
description: A case in which the Court held the judiciary did not have jurisdiction over DaimlerChrysler AG in California because the conduct in question was not in the state.

name: Heimeshoff v. Hartford Life & Accident Insurance Co.
description: A case in which the Court held that the Employment Retirement Income Security Act does not mandate a statute of limitations, allowing both parties in an insurance suit to mutually agree on a timeframe in which civil suits may be brought to court.

name: Atlantic Marine Construction Company v. U.S. District Court for the Western District of Texas
description: A case in which the Court held that the Federal Rules of Procedure allow two opposing parties in a lawsuit to transfer the litigation to a more convenient forum rather than being dismissed entirely.

name: United States v. Woods
description: A case in which the Court held that, under the Tax Equity and Fiscal Responsibility Act of 1982, a court in partnership-level proceedings has the right to consider the applicability of any penalty that relates to the partnership.

name: Burt v. Titlow
description: A case in which the Court held that the Antiterrorism and Effective Death Penalty Act  requires the Court of Appeals to apply a “doubly-deferential” standard in which both the state court and the defense attorney are given the benefit of the doubt in murder cases.

name: McCutcheon v. Federal Election Commission
description: A case in which the Court ruled that the two-year aggregate campaign contribution limit of the Bipartisan Campaign Reform Act was unconstitutional.

name: Madigan v. Levin
description: A case which the Court dismissed concerning whether the Age Discrimination Employment Act prevents state employees from seeking redress under the Equal Protection Clause and the Civil Rights Act.

name: Chadbourne and Parke LLP v. Troice
description: A case in which the Court held that the Securities Litigation Uniform Standards Act does not extend its scope beyond misrepresentations that are material to the sale of a closed financial security.

name: Metrish v. Lancaster
description: A case in which the Court held that eliminating the diminished capacity defense retroactively was reasonable.

name: University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center v. Nassar
description: A case in which the Court found that Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 requires the plaintiff to prove their employer would not have taken an action but for the existence of improper motives.

name: Sekhar v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that attempting to compel a person to issue a recommendation does not constitute extortion under the Hobbs Act.

name: Tarrant Regional Water District v. Herrmann
description: A case in which the Court held that Congress’ approval of an interstate water compact does not violate the Commerce Clause and that the compact does respect state lines.

name: Agency for International Development v. Alliance for Open Society International
description: A case in which the Court held that it was a violation of the First Amendment to withhold funding from non-government organizations if they did not institute an anti-prostitution policy.

name: Hillman v. Maretta
description: A case in which the Court found that the Federal Employees' Group Life Insurance Act preempts a Virginia state law regarding beneficiary designation upon divorce.

name: United States v. Kebodeaux
description: A case in which the Court held that the Necessary and Proper Clause gave Congress the power to create federal crimes and regulate their punishment, as well as apply the Sex Offender Registration and Notification Act (SORNA) on a defendant.

name: Salinas v. Texas
description: A case in which the Court held that the Fifth Amendment's Self-Incrimination clause does not protect individuals that have not been arrested.

name: American Trucking Associations v. City of Los Angeles
description: A case in which the Court held that when a municipal government is acting as a contract-based participant in the market, as opposed to a market regulator, it could not regulate motor carrier activities.

name: Adoptive Couple v. Baby Girl
description: A case in which the Court held that a non-custodial parent cannot stop an adoption made lawfully by a non-Indian parent by invoking the ICWA.

name: United States v. Davila
description: A case in which the Court held that a magistrate judge's improper participation in plea discussions does not warrant vacating a guilty plea.

name: Association for Molecular Pathology v. Myriad Genetics
description: A case in which the Court held that naturally occurring genes cannot be patented, but a creation of a new product in a lab could be patented.

name: United States v. Windsor
description: A case in which the Court found that the Defense of Marriage Act (DOMA) was unconstitutional under the equal protection clause of the Fifth Amendment.

name: Hollingsworth v. Perry
description: A case in which the Court found that the proponents of California's same-sex marriage ban (Proposition 8) do not have standing to appeal the decision that made Proposition 8 unconstitutional.

name: FTC v. Actavis Inc.
description: A case in which the Court found that antitrust law applies to reverse payment agreements.

name: Oxford Health Plans v. Sutter
description: A case in which the Court held that an arbitrator did not exceed his power when he interpreted that the parties intended, even if not explicitly, to authorize class-wide arbitration.

name: Dan's City Used Cars v. Pelkey
description: A case in which the Court found that the Federal Aviation Administration Authorization Act does not override state law regarding transportation of property.

name: Horne v. Department of Agriculture
description: A case in which the Court held the Takings Clause must be evaluated under the capacity in which the Government fines, and the citizens do not need to file a Takings Clause challenge in the Court of Federal Claims.

name: Sebelius v. Cloer
description: A case in which the Court found that a person who petitions under the National Childhood Vaccine Injury Act can recover attorney's fees regardless of if the petition was ultimately successful.

name: Mutual Pharmaceutical Co. v. Bartlett
description: A case in which the Court found that federal law preempts state law design-defect claims.

name: Arizona v. Inter Tribal Council of Arizona
description: A case in which the Court found the National Voter Registration Act preempted other voter registration requirements.

name: Bullock v. BankChampaign
description: A case in which the Court held that debts arising out of fraud or defalcation in a fiduciary capacity are not dischargeable in bankruptcy proceedings.

name: Shelby County v. Holder
description: A case in which the Court found that Section 4 of the Voting Rights Act was unconstitutional.

name: American Express Co., et al. v. Italian Colors Restaurant
description: A case in which the Court held that a clause prohibiting class action suits was enforceable even though it would cause costly arbitration.

name: Peugh v. United States
description: A case in which the Court found that using the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines at the time of the sentencing for a crime rather than at the time of the offense is a violation of the ex post facto clause.

name: Maryland v. King
description: A case in which the Court found that taking a DNA sample from people who are arrested, but not yet convicted, of a serious crime is not a violation of the Fourth Amendment.

name: McQuiggin v. Perkins
description: A case in which the Court held that proving actual innocence allows a petitioner to pursue habeas corpus relief regardless of a statute of limitations.

name: Trevino v. Thaler
description: A case in which the Court found that procedural default will not bar a federal court from hearing a claim of ineffective assistance of trial counsel.

name: PPL Corporation v. Commissioner of Internal Revenue
description: A case in which the Court held that courts should use a common-sense, substance-based approach instead of a formalistic approach when considering the effect of a foreign tax.

name: McBurney v. Young
description: A case in which the Court found that under the Privileges and Immunities clause and the Dormant Commerce clause, a state can deny access to its public records to citizens of another state.

name: Millbrook v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that claims against the United States for the intentional torts of prison officials is not limited to violations made during searches, seizures, or arrests.

name: Bowman v. Monsanto
description: A case in which the Court held that even after its authorized purchase, the reproduction and reuse of a seed violated the patent of the seed.

name: City of Arlington v. FCC
description: A case in which the Court found that the courts must apply the Chevron doctrine and defer to an agency's interpretation of its jurisdiction when that jurisdiction is called into question.

name: Gunn v. Minton
description: A case in which the Court found that even though federal courts have exclusive jurisdiction over patent law cases, state courts can still hear cases related to patent law as long as that it is not the primary issue.

name: Levin v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that the Gonzalez Act made an exception to the Federal Tort Claims Act by saying that a claim of the intentional tort of battery may be brought against an armed forces physician.

name: Koontz v. St. John's River Water Management
description: A case in which the Court held that the government may not conditionally approve land-use permits unless the conditions are connected and approximately proportionate to the effects of the proposed land use.

name: Alleyne v. United States
description: A case in which the Court found that a defendant cannot be found guilty of a claim not included in the indictment.

name: Boyer v. Louisiana
description: A case in which the Court was asked to decide whether a state's failure to fund counsel for an indigent defendant for five years should be weighed against the state in violation of the right to a speedy trial.

name: Missouri v. McNeely
description: A case in which the Court held that the Fourth Amendment protects against the warrantless taking of a blood sample under exigent circumstances.

name: Maracich v. Spears
description: A case in which the Court found that lawyers may use personal information protected by the Driver's Privacy Protection Act to find potential plaintiffs for a group action.

name: Wos v. E.M.A. et al.
description: A case in which the Court held that federal law preempts North Carolina's state law regarding reimbursement of medical expenses from a patient's settlement.

name: Gabelli v. Securities and Exchange Commission
description: A case in which the Court held that a five-year statute of limitations period begins at the time the violation is committed.

name: Standard Fire Insurance Company v. Knowles
description: A case in which the Court held that a plaintiff in a class action case cannot stipulate that the potential damages are less than $5 million in order to remove the case from federal jurisdiction.

name: Descamps v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that it was improper to apply the categorical approach in which the courts apply elements of a prior conviction with elements of a generic crime in order to enhance a sentence under the ACCA.

name: Chafin v. Chafin
description: A case in which the Court decided that the return of a child to his or her country of residence pursuant to The Hague Convention, does not make an appeal of that order moot.

name: Sebelius v. Auburn Regional Medical Center
description: A case in which the Court held that the statute of limitations for filing a claim with the Provider Reimbursement Review Board may be extended up to 3 years.

name: Los Angeles County Flood Control District v. Natural Resources Defense Council, Inc.
description: A case in which the Court found that transferring polluted water from one portion of a waterway to another portion of the same waterway did not constitute pollution under the Clean Water Act.

name: Decker v. Northwest Environmental Defense Center
description: A case in which the Court found that based on the Clean Water Act, a permit is not necessary for storm water runoff because it is not associated with industrial activity.

name: Genesis Healthcare v. Symczyk
description: A case in which the Court held that a collective action suit on behalf of other "similarly situated" employees becomes moot when the individual claim does.

name: Henderson v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that the determination of “plain error” is made during the appellate review, not during the trial.

name: US Airways v. McCutchen
description: A case in which the Court held that when a contract is silent on allocation of relief, the parties' intentions are best determined by the common-fund doctrine.

name: FTC v. Phoebe Putney Health System
description: A case in which the Court found state-action immunity does not apply if the state's legislature did not clearly articulate intent to allow anticompetitive activity through the Hospital Authorities Act.

name: Vance v. Ball State University
description: A case in which the Court held that, for purposes of liability for workplace harassment, the definition of "supervisor" is limited to a person empowered to take tangible employment action against the victim.

name: Marx v. General Revenue Corporation
description: A case in which the Court held that the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure awards costs to the prevailing party unless a statute explicitly states otherwise.

name: Already LLC v. Nike
description: A case in which the Court held that a covenant not to sue invalidates a company’s counterclaim for trademark enforcement.

name: Evans v. Michigan
description: A case in which the Court held that the Double Jeopardy clause bars a second trial even if the acquittal of the first trial was done in error.

name: Smith v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that the burden lies on the defendant, instead of the government, to prove withdrawal from a conspiracy regardless of when the withdrawal took place.

name: Amgen Inc. v. Connecticut Retirement Plans and Trust Funds
description: A case in which the Court held that during class certification, the court does not need proof of materiality and does not have to allow the defendant to present evidence to rebut the certification.

name: Comcast v. Behrend
description: A case in which the Court found that district courts cannot certify a class without adequate admissible evidence that damages may be measured and quantified on a class-wide basis.

name: Bailey v. United States
description: A case in which the Court found that once an individual left the premises after being searched under a legal search warrant, the individual's detainment must be justified by means other than the warrant.

name: Chaidez v. United States
description: A case in which the Court found that the Padilla rule created an entirely new rule regarding ineffective assistance of counsel and therefore did not apply to persons whose conviction became final before its announcement.

name: Florida v. Jardines
description: A case in which the Court found that a police officer and narcotic-sniffing dog entering the porch of a home constitutes a search and, without a warrant, is a violation of the Fourth Amendment.

name: Florida v. Harris
description: A case in which the Court found that police officers do not need to show evidence of a drug-detection dog's reliability to prove probable cause.

name: Kirtsaeng v. John Wiley & Sons, Inc.
description: A case in which the Court found that there is not geographical restriction on the "first sale" copyright doctrine.

name: Clapper v. Amnesty International USA
description: A case in which the Court held that the respondents lacked Article III standing against FISA because fear of intercepted communication and costs incurred to avoid intercepted communications are not injuries.

name: Fisher v. University of Texas
description: A case in which the Court held that the use of race in college admissions is constitutional under the Fourteenth Amendment only if applied with "strict judicial scrutiny."

name: Moncrieffe v. Holder
description: A case in which the Court found that distribution of small amounts of marijuana does not constitute an aggravated felony and thus, does not require deportation of the distributor.

name: Ryan v. Gonzales
description: A case in which the Court held that no right to competence exists during federal habeas corpus proceedings.

name: Arkansas Game & Fish Commission v. United States of America
description: A case in which the Court held the Fifth Amendment's Taking Clause could be enacted when a temporary flood regime destroyed property.

name: Johnson v. Williams
description: A case in which the Court found that an entire claim can be "adjudicated on its merits" even if the federal law claim was not expressly addressed.

name: United States v. Bormes
description: A case in which the Court held that the Little Tucker Act does not apply to lawsuits brought under the Federal Credit Reporting Act.

name: Kloeckner v Solis
description: A case in which the Court found that the district court, rather than the Court of Appeals, has jurisdiction over "mixed" cases that have been dismissed by the Merit Systems Protection Board.

name: Lozman v. Riviera Beach
description: A case in which the Court held that the definition of vessel under 1 U.S.C. §3 is too broad and not any floating structure is considered a vessel.

name: Arizona v. United States
description: A case in which the Court found that Arizona's state immigration provisions conflicted in part with federal immigration laws.

name: Match-E-Be-Nash-She-Wish Band v. Patchak
description: A case in which the Court held that a neighbor of a proposed Indian casino had standing to sue the government for taking 147 acres of a town's land under Section 465 of the Indian Reorganization Act.

name: RadLAX Gateway Hotel v. Amalgamated Bank
description: A case in which the Court held that a company could not obtain confirmation of a Chapter 11 bankruptcy plan that provided for the sale of its assets free from lien without permitting a bank to credit-bid at the sale.

name: Salazar v. Ramah Navajo Chapter
description: A case in which the Court held that, under the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act, the government is required to pay all of the contract support costs incurred by a tribal contractor if payment of those costs would exceed the statutory cap on the appropriations available to pay them.

name: Dorsey v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that criminals who had committed drug crimes before the passage of the Fair Sentencing Act of 2010 but were sentenced after its passage were entitled to the sentencing provisions laid out in the Act.

name: Christopher v. SmithKline
description: A case in which the Court held that the Secretary of Labor's definition of "outside salesman" apply to pharmaceutical sales representatives under the Fair Labor Standards Act.

name: National Federation of Independent Business v. Sebelius
description: Cases in which the Court held that the minimum coverage requirement of the Affordable Care Act was constitutional, that Congress had the power to enforce the taxation of most Americans that did not buy the minimum level of coverage, and that the federal government exceeded its power by pressuring States into accepting conditions that Congress could not impose directly by threatening to withhold all federal funding under Medicaid.

name: Vasquez v. United States
description: A case which the Court dismissed regarding whether or not the Seventh Circuit violated Supreme Court precedent on harmless error by focusing its analysis solely on the weight of untainted evidence, without considering any potential effects of the error.

name: Reichle v. Howards
description: A case in which the Court held that police officers and federal agents cannot be sued for violating someone’s rights, as long as the right that was supposedly violated was not formally recognized to exist at the time the officers acted.

name: Miller v. Alabama
description: A case in which the Court found it to be a violation of the Eighth Amendment to impose a sentence of life imprisonment without the possibility of parole on juvenile offenders.

name: Astrue v. Capato
description: A case in which the Court held that twins, born through in vitro fertilization after the death of their biological father, were not "children" under Title II of the Social Security act.

name: Southern Union Company v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that the rule applied in Apprendi v. New Jersey, where the Sixth Amendment’s guarantee of a jury trial requires that any fact which increases the maximum punishment for a particular crime be proved to a jury, applies to the imposition of criminal fines.

name: Armour v. City of Indianapolis
description: A case in which the Court held that an Indiana town did not violate residents' Fourteenth Amendment rights when it denied them reimbursement for paying property assessment fees, later deemed to be more than necessary, in full.

name: Mohamad v. Palestinian Authority
description: A case in which the Court held that the word "individual" in the Torture Victim Protection Act means a natural person and does not impose any liability against organizations.

name: Kiobel v. Royal Dutch Petroleum
description: A case in which the Court found that the Alien Tort Statute does not give ground for United States law to be applied extraterrestrially to other sovereign nations with their own laws.

name: Wood v. Milyard
description: A case in which the Court held that, under Day v. McDonough, appellate courts have the authority, though not the obligation, to raise a forfeited statute of limitations defense on its own.

name: Elgin v. Department of the Treasury
description: A case in which the Court held that the Civil Service Reform Act precludes federal courts' jurisdiction in cases where federal employees seek equitable relief.

name: United States v. Alvarez
description: A case in which the Court found that the Stolen Valor Act violated the First Amendment.

name: Blueford v. Arkansas
description: A case in which the Court held that an Arkansas man's rights against double jeopardy were not violated after his first murder trial was dismissed when the jury could not agree on a conviction charge.

name: Freeman v. Quicken Loans, Inc.
description: A case in which the Court held that Section 8(b) of the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act prohibits a real estate service provider from charging an unearned fee if the fee is divided between two or more parties.

name: Taniguchi v. Kan Pacific Saipan
description: A case in which the Court held that the winner of a federal-court lawsuit cannot be reimbursed by the losing party for any document translation costs under 28 U.S.C. § 1920(6).

name: Vartelas v. Holder
description: A case in which the Court held that 8 U.S.C. § 1101(a)(13)(C)(v) cannot be applied retroactively to a lawful permanent resident who pleads guilty to a crime prior to the effective date of the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act.

name: Holder v. Gutierrez
description: A case in which the Court held that an unemancipated minor cannot use his or her parent's years of residency to fulfill the requirements for having a removal from the country stayed under 8 U.S. C. 1229(a).

name: United States v. Home Concrete & Supply
description: A case in which the Court held that section 6501(e)(1)(A) of the Internal Revenue Code does not apply when a taxpayer overstates the amount of property that he has sold, which then understates the gain received from the sale.

name: Filarsky v. Delia
description: A case in which the Court found that a private attorney retained by a governmental agency is not prevented from claiming qualified immunity simply because they are not a full-time employee of the agency.

name: Roberts v. Sea-Land Services
description: A case in which the Court held that the Longshore Act sets the period when an injured worker is awarded disability compensation as the fiscal year when the worker first becomes entitled to compensation.

name: Coleman v. Maryland Court of Appeals
description: A case in which the Court held that states have sovereign immunity to suits brought under the self-care provision of the Family and Medical Leave Act.

name: FCC v. Fox Television Stations
description: A case in which the Court determined that an FCC policy regarding profane language was too vague, and which was remanded to the Second Circuit Court of Appeals to determine if the FCC violated its customers' First Amendment rights.

name: Knox v. Service Employees International Union
description: A case in which the Court found that, under the First Amendment, public-sector unions are not permitted to impose a special assessment fee without the consent of the member upon whom it is imposed.

name: Sackett v. EPA
description: A case in which the Court found that homeowners have a right to go to court over a Clean Water Act order of the Environmental Protection Agency.

name: Perry v. Perez
description: A case which the Court remanded regarding whether or not a Texas district court abused its discretion under the Voting Rights Act when it redrew 36 districts.

name: Kappos v. Hyatt
description: A case in which the Court held that a patent applicant's ability to introduce new evidence in a civil action against the Patent and Trademark Office was only limited by the Federal Rules of Evidence and the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure.

name: PPL Montana v. Montana
description: A case in which the Court held that the constitutional test for determining whether a section of a river is navigable for title purposes requires a trial court to determine whether the relevant stretch of the river was navigable at the time of statehood.

name: Mayo Collaborative Services v. Prometheus Laboratories, Inc.
description: A case in which the Court held that certain diagnostic medical tests are unpatentable products of nature.

name: Williams v. Illinois
description: A case in which the Court held that testimony of an expert witness that is based on a test an expert did not personally perform is admissible and does not violate a defendant's Sixth Amendment Confrontation Clause rights.

name: Martel v. Clair
description: A case in which the Court held that a condemned state prisoner in federal proceedings is not entitled to replace his court-appointed counsel with another court-appointed counsel due to dissatisfaction with the counsel's service.

name: Caraco Pharmaceutical Laboratories, Ltd. v. Novo Nordisk A/S
description: A case in which the Court held that counterclaims that challenge unpatented uses of generic drugs, even if other approved uses are still under patent, are allowable under the Hatch-Waxman Act.

name: Messerschmidt v. Millender
description: A case in which the Court held that qualified immunity protects government officials from civil liability when their conduct does not violate any clearly established right of which a reasonable person would have known.

name: FAA v. Cooper
description: A case in which the Court held that the Privacy Act of 1974 does not cover mental and emotional distress under "actual damages."

name: Setser v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that a federal judge has discretion to order a federal sentence to run consecutively or concurrently with an anticipated state sentence.

name: Credit Suisse Securities LLC v. Simmonds
description: A case in which the Court held that Section 16(b) of the 1934 Securities Exchange Act is subject to tolling, where tolling starts after the filing of a Section 16(a) claim.

name: Hall v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that assets sold by a debtor in bankruptcy proceedings does not count as a separately taxable estate in Chapter 12 bankruptcies.

name: Mims v. Arrow Financial Services, LLC
description: A case in which the Court held that the Telephone Consumer Protection Act does not strip federal courts of the ability to hear cases that would normally be brought in state courts.

name: First American Financial Corp. v. Edwards
description: A case which the Court dismissed, regarding whether or not a private purchaser of real estate services has standing to sue when a kickback does not affect the value or quality of the service.

name: Kurns v. Railroad Friction Products Corp.
description: A case in which the Court held that the Locomotive Inspection Act preempts state law design defect claims and state law failure to warn claims.

name: National Meat Association v. Harris
description: A case in which the Court held that a California law requiring slaughterhouses to "immediately euthanize" any nonambulatory animal on its premises is preempted by the Federal Meat Inspection Act.

name: Smith v. Cain
description: A case in which the Court held that the omission of eyewitness testimony in a murder trial, which was the only evidence linking the accused to the crime, was a violation of the accused's due process.

name: United States v. Jones
description: A case in which the Court found that a police department's placement of a GPS tracking device on a man's Jeep without his knowledge was an illegal search under the Fourth Amendment.

name: Zivotofsky v. Clinton
description: A case in which the Court held that a dispute over passport regulation was not a political issue and is thus liable for judicial review.

name: Kawashima v. Holder
description: A case in which the Court held that filing a false tax return in violation of 26 U.S.C. Section 7206 qualifies as an aggravated felony under the Immigration and Nationality Act if the Government's revenue loss exceeds $10,000.

name: Perry v. New Hampshire
description: A case in which the Court held that the Due Process Clause does not require a preliminary inquiry into the reliability of an eyewitness' identification unless the ID was brought about under unnecessarily suggestive circumstances.

name: Gonzalez v. Thaler
