description: A case in which the Court held that a prisoner who does not seek review in a state’s highest court faces final judgment for the purposes of Section 2244(d)(1)(A) upon “expiration of the time for seeking such review.”

name: Minneci v. Pollard
description: A case in which the Court held that a prisoner cannot assert an Eighth Amendment claim for damages against private prison employees.

name: Rehberg v. Paulk
description: A case in which the Court held that a witness in a grand jury proceeding is entitled to the same absolute immunity from a §1983 action as a witness who testifies at trial.

name: Lafler v. Cooper
description: A case in which the Court found that the test to determine ineffective assistance of counsel, from Strickland v. Washington, was not properly applied in an aggravated assault case.

name: Missouri v. Frye
description: A case in which the Court held that the Sixth Amendment requires defense attorneys to communicate formal plea offers from the prosecution.

name: Florence v. Board of Chosen Freeholders of the County of Burlington
description: A case in which the Court held that prisons that conduct suspicion-less strip searches on incoming inmates do not violate the prisoner's Fourth Amendment rights.

name: Judulang v. Holder
description: A case in which the Court held that the policy used to determine whether a resident alien is able to ask for relief from deportation under a repealed portion of immigration laws is “arbitrary and capricious” under the Administrative Procedure Act, 5 U.S.C. § 706(2)(A).

name: Pacific Operators Offshore v. Valladolid
description: A case in which the Court held that the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act extends coverage for injuries that occurred as the result of operations conducted on the outer continental shelf to an employee, as long as the employee can establish a substantial connection between the injury and the employer’s extractive operations.

name: Greene v. Fisher
description: A case in which the Court held that decisions of the Court do not constitute "clearly established federal law" if the decision predates the decision of a relevant state court.

name: CompuCredit Corp. v. Greenwood
description: A case in which the Court held that the Credit Repair Organizations Act does not give credit card users the right to bring a suit against their card companies in court.

name: Hosanna-Tabor Evangelical Lutheran Church and School v. EEOC
description: A case in which the Court found that a woman employed by a religious school who taught daily religion classes, was a commissioned minister, and regularly lead students in prayer and worship, did not have grounds to sue the school under the Ministerial Exception.

name: Golan v. Holder
description: A case in which the Court held that Section 514 of the Uruguay Round Agreements Act, regarding copyright status of works in the public domain, does not violate the Copyright Clause or the First Amendment.

name: Howes v. Fields
description: A case in which the Court held that a prisoner, currently held in jail, did not have his Miranda rights violated when he was questioned inside the jail for a different crime.

name: Maples v. Thomas
description: A case in which the Court found that a prisoner's attorneys abandoning his case without informing him was a reasonable excuse to prevent the prisoner from having an appeal denied due to a failure to file a motion in advance of the deadline.

name: Martinez v. Ryan
description: A case in which the Court held that a defendant who is prohibited by state law from raising a claim of ineffective assistance of counsel may establish cause for such a claim at trial by showing evidence of ineffective assistance up to that point.

name: Douglas v. Independent Living Center of Southern California
description: A case which the Court remanded to the Ninth Circuit regarding whether or not federal law preempts state reductions in Medicaid payments.

name: Reynolds v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that under the Sex Offender Registration and Notification Act, pre-Act offenders are not obligated to register without affirmative action of the Attorney General.

name: Nevada Commission on Ethics v. Carrigan
description: A case in which the Court held that the Nevada law requiring elected officials to disqualify themselves when they are asked to vote on matters that present a conflict of interest was constitutional.

name: Sorrell v. IMS Health Inc.
description: A case in which the Court held that a Vermont statute banning the sale, transmission or use of prescription drug user data violated protected speech of the pharmaceutical research companies, manufacturers and others who use that data.

name: Erica P. John Fund, Inc. v. Halliburton Co.
description: A case in which the Court held that securities fraud plaintiffs need not prove loss causation in order to obtain class certification.

name: McNeill v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that a federal sentencing court must determine whether an offense under state law is a "serious drug offense" within the meaning of the Armed Career Criminal Act by consulting the maximum sentence applicable at the time of the defendant's conviction.

name: United States v. Jicarilla Apache Nation
description: A case in which the Court held that the fiduciary exception to the attorney-client privilege does not apply to the general trust relationship between the United States and the Indian Tribes.

name: American Electric Power Co., Inc. v. Connecticut
description: A case in which the Court that held the Clean Air Act bars suits by governmental bodies and private parties seeking to curb emissions from utilities via the federal common law.

name: Tapia v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that a district court may not give a defendant a longer prison sentence based on speculation about if and when the defendant would be able to participate in an inmate drug rehabilitation program.

name: Microsoft Corp. v. i4i Limited Partnership
description: A case in which the Court held that a challenge to a patent's validity must offer clear and convincing evidence.

name: PLIVA, Inc. v. Mensing
description: A case in which the Court held that generic drug makers cannot be sued for not warning about potentially dangerous side effects on their drug labels, even when they follow federal rules that only require their labels to match those of their brand-name equivalents.

name: Talk America, Inc. v. Michigan Bell Telephone Co.
description: A case in which the Court held that federal law requires local telephone companies to allow new competitors in their markets to link to their existing networks through connecting wires at low, government-regulated rates.

name: Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. v. Dukes
description: A case in which the Court held that the small group who initiated a lawsuit could not represent all of Wal-Mart's female employees, and therefore could not bring a class action lawsuit against Wal-Mart.

name: Fowler v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that in order to prove a criminal violation of the federal witness tampering statute when a defendant allegedly kills a witness, the government must prove that the victim would have provided information regarding the crime.

name: CSX Transportation v. McBride
description: Question: Does the Federal Employers' Liability Act require proof of proximate causation?

name: Arizona Free Enterprise Club's Freedom Club PAC v. Bennett
description: A case in which the Court held that the Arizona campaign finance law linking public financing for candidates to the amount spent by their opponents violated the First Amendment's protection of political speech.

name: J.D.B. v. North Carolina
description: A case in which the Court ruled that courts should consider the age of a juvenile suspect in deciding whether he or she is in custody for Miranda purposes.

name: Turner v. Rogers
description: A case in which the Court held that a defendant facing incarceration for civil contempt does not have a constitutional right to a court-appointed attorney under the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.

name: Fox v. Vice
description: A case in which the Court held that a court may award attorney's fees to civil rights defendants when the plaintiff's suit involves frivolous and non-frivolous claims, but only for the costs incurred due to the frivolous claims.

name: Borough of Duryea v. Guarnieri
description: A case in which the Court held that state and local government employees may not sue their employers for retaliation under the First Amendment's Petition Clause when they petition the government on matters of private concern.

name: Tolentino v. New York
description: A case the Court dismissed, which would have considered whether an individual's motor vehicle records may be used as evidence if the police consulted those records only after making an illegal stop of the individual's vehicle.

name: Davis v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that the good-faith exception to the exclusionary rule applies to a search that was authorized by precedent at the time of the search, but was subsequently ruled unconstitutional.

name: Ashcroft v. Al-Kidd
description: A case in which the Court held that former Attorney General John Ashcroft was entitled to qualified immunity.

name: Bullcoming v. New Mexico
description: A case in which the Court held that a blood-alcohol test admitted without the actual testimony of the person who prepared the results violates a criminal defendant's Sixth Amendment rights under the Confrontation Clause.

name: Schindler Elevator Corp. v. United States ex rel. Kirk
description: A case in which the Court held that a whistleblower may not use information obtained through Freedom of Information Act requests to allege violations of the Federal Claims Act by a government contractor.

name: Camreta v. Greene
description: A case which the Court vacated in part and remanded in favor of the defendant without addressing the Fourth Amendment question at issue.

name: Board of Trustees of the Leland Stanford Junior University v. Roche Molecular Systems, Inc.
description: A case in which the Court held that patents on inventions that arise from federally-funded research do not automatically go to university where the inventor worked.

name: DePierre v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that the term "cocaine base" encompasses every form of cocaine that is classified chemically as a base.

name: Freeman v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that a federal judge has the authority to reduce a criminal sentence after the U.S. Sentencing Commission amended the Sentencing Guidelines if the judge has already accepted a plea agreement.

name: Global-Tech Appliances, Inc. v. SEB S.A.
description: A case in which the Court ruled that induced infringement under the patent clause requires knowledge that the induced acts constitute patent infringement.

name: Bond v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that a defendant, convicted under a federal statute, has a right to challenge his/her conviction based on the unconstitutionality of the statute.

name: United States  v. Tinklenberg
description: A case in which the Court held that the time between the filing of a pretrial motion and its disposition is excluded from the deadline for commencing trial under the Speedy Trial Act.

name: FCC v. AT&T Inc.
description: A case in which the Court held that corporations do not have a right of personal privacy that would prevent the disclosure of public records handed over to federal agencies.

name: Astra USA v. Santa Clara County
description: A case in which the Court held that health care providers cannot sue drug makers for overcharging public hospitals for prescription drugs.

name: General Dynamics Corp. v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that neither the government nor the contractor could pursue litigation because of the risk that state secrets might be revealed.

name: Smith v. Bayer Corp.
description: A case in which the Court held that the federal court exceeded its authority under the relitigation exception to the Anti-Injunction Act when it prevented a group of plaintiffs from proceeding with a class-action lawsuit over a cholesterol-lowering drug.

name: Stern v. Marshall
description: A case in which the Court held that the Bankruptcy Court did not have the constitutional authority to enter judgement on the petitioner's counterclaim.

name: Sykes v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that a conviction for resisting arrest counts as a violent felony under the Armed Career Criminal Act.

name: Kentucky v. King
description: A case in which the Court held the exclusionary rule, which forbids the use of illegally seized evidence except in emergency situations, applies when the emergency is created by lawful police action.

name: Goodyear Dunlop Tires Operations, S.A. v. Brown
description: A case in which the Court held that a consumer cannot sue a manufacturer in a U.S. court when the manufacturer's only connection with the U.S. is that another company sells its products in the country.

name: J. McIntyre Machinery, Ltd. v. Nicastro
description: A case in which the Court held that a consumer cannot sue a foreign manufacturer in state court over a product that the foreign company marketed and sold in the United States.

name: Matrixx Initiatives, Inc. v. Siracusano
description: A case in which the Court held that a plaintiff could state a claim based on a pharmaceutical company's non-disclosure of adverse event reports, even though the reports are not alleged to be statistically significant.

name: Montana v. Wyoming and North Dakota
description: A case in which the Court held that Montana did not violate the Yellowstone River Compact by leaving less water in the river for Montana's uses.

name: Chamber of Commerce of the United States v. Whiting
description: A case in which the Court held that Arizona laws requiring employers to verify the employment eligibility of their employees through a federal database was not unconstitutional.

name: Chase Bank USA v. McCoy
description: A case in which the Court held that the Truth In Lending Act did not require Chase Bank to provide notice of interest rate increases that occurred because of customer default.

name: Thompson v. North American Stainless, LP
description: A case in which the Court held that an employer violates Title VII of the Civil Rights Acts by firing the fiancee of an employee who complains about workplace discrimination.

name: Janus Capital Group, Inc. v. First Derivative Traders
description: A case in which the Court held that a service provider cannot be held liable for statements for which they are not directly responsible.

name: Pepper v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that when a defendant's sentence has been set aside on appeal, a district court may consider evidence of the defendant's rehabilitation after the initial sentences, which may support lesser sentencing guidelines.

name: Henderson v. Shinseki
description: A case in which the Court held that missing the deadline for filing a notice of appeal with the Veterans Court did not bar a plaintiff from making a claim.

name: Virginia Office for Protection and Advocacy v. Stewart
description: A case in which the Court held that a federal court may hear a lawsuit for prospective injunctive relief against state officials brought by another agency of the same state.

name: Milner v. Department of the Navy
description: A case in which the Court held that documents related to the effect of explosions from Navy exercises did not qualify for withholding under Exception 2 of the Freedom of Information Act.

name: CIGNA v. Amara
description: A case in which the Court held that the U.S. District Court for the District of Connecticut did not have the authority to reform CIGNA's pension plan.

name: Brown v. Plata
description: A case in which the Court held that a court order requiring California to reduce its prison population to remedy unconstitutional conditions in its correctional facilities did not violate the Prison Litigation Reform Act.

name: Walker v. Martin
description: A case in which the Court held that the California rule requiring state habeas petitions to be filed "as promptly as the circumstances allow" constitutes an independent state ground that is adequate to bar habeas relief in federal court.

name: Wall v. Kholi
description: A case in which the Court held that the one-year window of time in which an inmate may file a habeas challenge to their sentence in federal court after conviction is delayed while a state court considers an inmate's request for a sentence reduction.

name: CSX Transportation, Inc. v. Alabama Department of Revenue
description: A case in which the Court held that a railroad company could invoke the Railroad Revitalization and Regulatory Reform Act to challenge sales and use taxes that apply to rail carriers, but exempt their competitors in the transportation industry.

name: Flores-Villar v. United States
description: A case in which the Court affirmed the decision of the lower court without addressing the constitutional question at issue, which was whether Nguyen v. INS permit gender discrimination.

name: Cullen v. Pinholster
description: A case in which the Court held that a federal court could not overturn a state criminal conviction on the basis of the facts the defendant could have alleged, but did not, in state court.

name: AT&T Mobility LLC v. Concepcion
description: A case in which the Court held the Federal Arbitration Act preempts state laws that "stand as obstacles to the FAA's objectives."

name: Costco Wholesale Corporation v. Omega, S.A.
description: A case in which the Court held that the first-sale doctrine did not apply to imported goods manufactured abroad. This case set no new Supreme Court precedent.

name: Mayo Foundation v. United States
description: A case in which the Court upheld the Treasury Department's rule that treats medical residents as full-time employees, and therefore not exempt from the payment of payroll taxes.

name: Arizona Christian School Tuition Organization v. Winn
description: A case in which the Court held that the plaintiffs lacked standing because the Arizona tuition tax credit does not involve the appropriation or expenditure of state funds.

name: Williamson v. Mazda Motor of America, Inc.
description: A case in which the Court held that a wrongful death lawsuit under California law alleging that Mazda should have installed belt and shoulder seatbelts in the backseat of a minivan is not preempted by a federal regulation that gives automakers the option to install either kind of seatbelts.

name: Staub v. Proctor Hospital
description: A case in which the Court held that an employer may be found liable for the discriminatory acts of supervisors, who do not themselves make employment decisions but do influence the employment decision-makers.

name: Brown v. Entertainment Merchants Association
description: A case in which the Court held that video games, including violent ones, are protected speech under the First Amendment.

name: Sossamon v. Texas
description: A case in which the Court held that a person may not sue a state official in his individual capacity for damages under the Religious Land Use and Institutional Persons Act.

name: Ortiz v. Jordan
description: A case in which the Court held that a party may not appeal a denial of summary judgement after a district court has conducted a full trial on the merits.

name: United States v. Tohono O'odham Nation
description: A case in which the Court held that the Court of Federal Claims lacked jurisdiction to hear a suit against the federal government about a claim already being litigated against the government in another court, even when the lawsuits seek different relief based on the same set of facts.

name: Kasten v. Saint-Gobain Performance Plastics Corp.
description: A case in which the Court held that the Fair Labor Standards Act applies to a complaint, whether oral or written.

name: Skinner v. Switzer
description: A case in which the Court held that a convicted prisoner seeking access to biological evidence for DNA testing may assert that claim in a civil rights action under 42 U.S.C. § 1983.

name: Bruesewitz v. Wyeth Inc.
description: A case in which the Court held that the National Childhood Vaccine Injury Act shielded manufacturers from certain product liability lawsuits that seek damages for serious health problems suffered by children.

name: Premo v. Moore
description: A case in which the Court held that a lawyer does not provide inadequate representation by failing to seek repression of a client's confession before he pleads no contest to murder.

name: Harrington v. Richter
description: A case in which the Court held that a defense lawyer was not deficient for failing to consult blood evidence when planning strategy for trial.

name: Connick v. Thompson
description: A case in which the Court held that a prosecutor's office cannot be held liable for the illegal conduct of one of its employees when there has only been one violation resulting from allegedly deficient training.

name: Snyder v. Phelps
description: A case in which the Court held that the Westboro Baptist Church was protected under the First Amendment while picketing a military funeral.

name: Los Angeles County, CA v. Humphries
description: A case in which the Court held that plaintiffs seeking declaratory relief against a local public entity must demonstrate that the constitutional violation in question was the result of the public entity's policy, custom, or practice.

name: National Aeronautics and Space Administration v. Nelson
description: A case in which the Court held that the government's extended background checks for federal employees under the Bush administration's antiterrorism initiative did not violate an employee's constitutional right to privacy.

name: Michigan v. Bryant
description: A case in which the Court held that inquiries of wounded victims concerning the perpetrator are non-testimonial if they objectively indicate that the purpose of the interrogation is to enable police assistance to meet an ongoing emergency, and thus, are not afforded heightened protection.

name: Abbott v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that a defendant who receives a mandatory minimum sentence for using or carrying a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime can serve that sentence consecutively with any other term of imprisonment.

name: Ransom v. FIA Card Services, N.A.
description: A case in which the Court held that a debtor who does not make a loan or lease payment could not take the car-ownership deduction.

name: Doe #1 v. Reed
description: A case in which the Court held that requiring the disclosure of the names of individuals who sign a referendum petition does not violate the signers' First Amendment rights to protection of political speech.

name: Monsanto Co. v. Geertson Seed Farms
description: A case in which the Court held that a district court must conduct an evidentiary hearing to enter an injunction.

name: Rent-A-Center West, Inc. v. Jackson
description: A case in which the Court held that district courts are required in all cases to determine whether an arbitration agreement, subject to the Federal Arbitration Act, is unconscionable.

name: Hardt v. Reliance Standard Life Ins. Co.
description: A case in which the Court held that a party is entitled to attorneys' fees pursuant to Section 502(g)(1) of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act when an ERISA violation has occurred.

name: Krupski v. Costa Crociere, S.p.A.
description: A case in which the Court held that the Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals' interpretation of Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 15(c)(1)(C), which permits an amended complaint to relate back to when the amendment corrects a "mistake concerning the proper party's identity," undermined the fundamental purpose of the rule.

name: Dolan v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that federal courts may enter a restitution order beyond the time prescribed under the Mandatory Victims Restitution Act if certain qualifications are met.

name: City of Ontario v. Quon
description: A case in which the Court held that the city of Ontario's search of an employee's text messages did not violate his First Amendment rights because the search was not excessive in scope and was motivated by a legitimate work-related purpose.

name: Christian Legal Society Chapter v. Martinez
description: A case in which the Court held that a college's mandate requiring all officially-recognized student organizations be inclusive and welcoming to all students did not violate a group of Christian students' First Amendment rights when the college refused to recognize a student group that required all members to sign a statement of Christian beliefs for membership.

name: Carachuri-Rosendo v. Holder
description: A case in which the Court held that a minor drug offense is not automatic grounds for deportation of a legal immigrant.

name: Robertson v. United States ex rel. Watson
description: A case, which the Court dismissed as improvidently granted, concerning the constitutionality of actions of criminal contempt brought in the name and pursuant to the power of a private person, rather than in the name and pursuant to the power of the United States.

name: Dillon v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that federal sentencing guidelines are binding when a district court imposes a new sentence under a revised guideline range.

name: Barber v. Thomas
description: A case in which the Court held that the Federal Bureau of Prisons' method of determining "good behavior," which was based on the inmate's time in prison rather than the overall sentence, was constitutional.

name: Morrison v. National Australia Bank
description: A case in which the Court held that the Securities and Exchange Act does not provide a cause of action against foreign plaintiffs suing foreign and American defendants for misconduct in connection with securities traded on foreign stock exchanges.

name: Renico v. Lett
description: A case in which the Court held that a Michigan trial court did not properly apply established Supreme Court precedent in a murder trial.

name: Magwood v. Patterson
description: A case in which the Court held that, when a habeas corpus application alleges new judgment for the first time, it is not "second or successive" under the Antiterrorism and Effective Death Penalty Act and is therefore constitutional.

name: Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha Ltd. v. Regal-Beloit Corp.
description: A case in which the Court held that the Carmack Amendment of the Interstate Commerce Act does not apply to the inland leg of an international shipment.

name: New Process Steel v. NLRB
description: A case in which the Court held that the National Labor Relations Board cannot execute duties with only two members on its board when 29 U.S.C. Section 153(b) mandates that quorum for the board is three members.

name: Levin v. Commerce Energy, Inc.
description: A case in which the Court held that a taxpayer's complaint of allegedly discriminatory state taxation must proceed originally in state court.

name: Hamilton v. Lanning
description: A case in which the Court held that a bankruptcy court may take evidence into account that suggests a debtor's finances prior to the filing period would be different than the debtor's finances during the period of bankruptcy.

name: Samantar v. Yousuf
description: A case in which the Court held that the Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act does not extend to an individual acting in his official capacity on behalf of the foreign state.

name: Hui v. Castaneda
description: A case in which the Court held that the immunity granted by the Federal Tort Claims Act precludes Bivens actions against Public Health Service officers for constitutional violations committed while in the scope of the employees' official duties.

name: McDonald v. Chicago
description: A case in which the Court held that the Fourteenth Amendment makes the Second Amendment's right to bear arms for the purpose of self-defense applicable in the states.

name: Holland v. Florida
description: A case in which the Court held that a state prisoner who has exhausted their appeals process in their state has one year to file a writ of habeas corpus, with certain exceptions (including attorney misconduct) that may allow the courts to relax that deadline.

name: Berghuis v. Thompkins
description: A case in which the Court held that a Michigan state court did not deprive a prisoner of his Miranda rights or his right to effective counsel because he failed to state his defense of those rights "unambiguously."

name: Skilling v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that the former CEO of Enron received a fair trial before an impartial jury, and that the federal law that makes it a crime to deprive someone of a fair and honest trial only applies to bribery and kickback schemes.

name: United States v. Marcus
description: A case in which the Court held that an appellate court may correct an error not raised at trial only when the appellant demonstrates that: (1) there is an error; (2) the error is clear and obvious; (3) the error affected the appellant's substantial rights; and (4) the error seriously affects the fairness, integrity, or public reputation of judicial proceedings.

name: Carr v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that the Sex Offender and Registration Act does not apply to sex offenders' interstate travel that occurred before the Act's effective date.

name: Holder v. Humanitarian Law Project
description: A case in which the Court held that sections of the Antiterrorism and Effective Death Penalty Act were not unconstitutionally vague in a lawsuit that named the Kurdistan Workers Party and Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam.

name: United States v. O'Brien
description: A case in which the Court held that the fact that a firearm was a machine gun is an element to be proved to the jury beyond a reasonable doubt, not a sentencing factor to be proved to the judge at sentencing.

name: Astrue v. Ratliff
description: A case in which the Court determined that an award of attorney’s fees under the Equal Access to Justice Act can be used to offset the prevailing party’s preexisting debt to the government.

name: Lewis v. Chicago
description: A case in which the Court held that an employee may file a Title VII disparate impact claim within 300 days after their employer executes the allegedly unlawful practice.

name: Conkright v. Frommert
description: A case in which the Court held that the Second Circuit Court of Appeals erred when they did not hold a claim of unfair pension distribution by employees of the Xerox Corporation to a deferential standard of review.

name: Berghuis v. Smith
description: A case in which the Court held that a Michigan state court did not create an unfair bias in jury selection for a murder trial.

name: Mac's Shell Service v. Shell Oil Products Co.
description: A case in which the Court held that a franchise operator cannot successfully bring a claim of constructive termination of the franchise unless it can be proven that the parent company directly forced the franchise out of business.

name: Granite Rock Co. v. International Brotherhood of Teamsters
description: A case in which the Court held that federal courts have jurisdiction to determine whether or not a collective bargaining agreement was formed between two parties when the agreement is disputed, but neither party makes a challenge to the arbitration clause contained in the agreement.

name: American Needle Inc. v. National Football League
description: A case in which the Court held that separate teams in the NFL are not a collective, single entity, and that their actions regarding licensing their merchandise are subject to the Sherman Antitrust Act.

name: Jerman v. Carlisle, McNellie, Rini, Kramer, & Ulrich LPA
description: A case in which the Court held that a debt collector's mistake in interpreting the law cannot qualify for the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act bona fide error defense.

name: United States v. Comstock
description: A case in which the Court held that the Necessary and Proper Clause granted Congress authority to enact the Adam Walsh Protection and Safety Act.

name: Abbott v. Abbott
description: A case in which the Court held that the Hague Convention gave a father a right to have his child brought back to Chile from Texas after the child's mother violated her divorce agreement that required both parents' consent for the child to be taken out of Chile.

name: Briscoe v. Virginia
description: A case which the Court remanded regarding the Sixth Amendment rights of a man convicted of cocaine possession.

name: Alabama v. North Carolina
description: A case in which the Court held that Alabama did not have the power to impose monetary sanctions against North Carolina for violating a multi-state waste cleanup compact.

name: Stolt-Nielsen v. Animalfeeds International Corp.
description: A case in which the Court held that imposing class arbitration on parties who have not agreed to authorize class arbitration is inconsistent with the Federal Arbitration Act.

name: Black v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that a court of appeals may not retroactively impose a verdict preservation requirement that is not in the Federal Rules of Procedure.

name: Weyhrauch v. United States
description: A case which the Court remanded to the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals for further proceedings in light of its decision in Skilling v. United States.

name: Florida v. Powell
description: A case in which the Court held that a Florida police officer did not invalidate a convicted felon's Miranda rights during his arrest.

name: Free Enterprise Fund v. Public Company Oversight Board
description: A case in which the Court held that the Sarbanes-Oxley Act violated the Appointment Clause of the Constitution.

name: Stop the Beach Renourishment Inc. v. Florida Department of Environmental Protection
description: A case in which the Court held that a ruling on littoral ("on or near the shore") takings by the Florida Supreme Court did not cause a judicial takings violation of the Fifth or Fourteenth Amendments.

name: Milavetz, Gallop & Milavetz, P.A. v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that attorneys who provide bankruptcy assistance are debt relief agencies under the Bankruptcy Abuse Prevention and Consumer Protection Act.

name: United Student Aid Funds Inc. v. Espinosa
description: A case in which the Court held that Chapter 13 bankruptcy plans which discharge student loans are not void if the debtor fails to provide evidence of "undue hardship" in an adversary proceeding.

name: Graham County Soil and Water Conservation District v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that an audit performed by a state or its political subdivisions constitutes an administrative report within the False Claims Act.

name: Merck & Co. v. Reynolds
description: A case in which the Court held that a statute of limitations begins to run once a plaintiff actually discovers -- or a reasonably diligent plaintiff would have discovered -- the facts constituting the violation in the present case, whichever comes first.

name: Kucana v. Holder
description: A case in which the Court held that 8 U.S.C. Section 1252(a)(2)(B)(ii) does not preclude federal courts from hearing cases specified by the Attorney General, only cases that are specified by statute.

name: Hertz Corp. v. Friend
description: A case in which the Court held that the court system cannot disregard the location of a corporation's principal place of business in a multi-state lawsuit.

name: Bilski v. Kappos
description: A case in which the Court held that the "machine-or-transformation" test adopted by the Patent and Trademark Office (PTO) was a legal means for determining patent eligibility.

name: Graham v. Florida
description: A case in which the Court found that a non-homicidal conviction leading to a life sentence without parole for a juvenile violates the Eighth Amendment.

name: Sullivan v. Florida
description: A case, which the Court dismissed as improvidently granted, concerning the constitutionality of imposing a life sentence with no chance of parole on a 13-year-old convicted of a non-homicidal offense.

name: Pottawattamie County v. McGhee
description: A case which the Court dismissed before argument concerning whether or not a prosecutor can be subject to civil prosecution for allegedly violating a criminal defendants' substantial due process rights by fabricating evidence and then introducing that evidence at trial.

name: Wood v. Allen
description: A case in which the Court held that an inmate's conviction was proper, despite the fact that his attorney failed to properly investigate or introduce evidence that his IQ was well below average.

name: NRG Power Marketing, LLC v. Maine Pub. Util. Comm'n
description: A case in which the Court held that the Mobile-Sierra doctrine, which is premised on the existence of a "voluntary contract" between parties, applies to non-parties in a Federal Energy Regulatory Commission settlement.

name: Hemi Group LLC v. City of New York
description: A case in which the Court held that the city of New York had standing to sue out-of-state cigarette vendors under the Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act.

name: Schwab v. Reilly
description: A case in which the Court held that someone who files for bankruptcy is allowed to retain the value of certain property that would otherwise be sold to pay off debts, up to a certain dollar limit; if the value of the property is more than the individual in bankruptcy estimated, the value above the pre-determined limit may be used to pay creditors.

name: Jones v. Harris Associates L.P.
description: A case in which the Court held that Section 36(b) of the Investment Company Act requires a determination that the financial adviser charges a fee that is "so disproportionately large is bears no reasonable relationship to the services rendered" before legal action may be taken.

name: Beard v. Kindler
description: A case which the Court vacated due to lack of jurisdiction concerning whether or not the Pennsylvania fugitive waiver rule could preclude habeas corpus review.

name: Shady Grove Orthopedic Associates, P.A. v. Allstate Insurance Co.
description: A case in which the Court held that Section 901(b) of the New York Rules of Civil Procedure does not preclude a federal court ruling on entities from different jurisdictions from hearing a class action under Rule 23 of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure.

name: Perdue v. Kenny A.
description: A case in which the Court held that reasonable attorneys' fees awarded under a federal fee-shifting statute can be enhanced based on the quality of the attorney's performance and results obtained in exceptional circumstances.

name: Alvarez v. Smith
description: A case which the Court dismissed regarding property seizure under the Illinois Drug Asset Forfeiture Procedure Act (DAFPA).

name: South Carolina v. North Carolina
description: A case in which the Court held that a North Carolina city could not intervene in a South Carolina city's use of a river that originated in North Carolina but flowed into South Carolina.

name: Smith v. Spisak
description: A case in which the Court held that the 1983 conviction of a man for murder was not unconstitutional, because it did not require the jury to unanimously find the existence of any mitigating factor, which Mills v. Maryland forbids.

name: Padilla v. Kentucky
description: A case in which the Court held that counsel must inform a client whether or not his plea carries a risk of deportation under the Sixth Amendment.

name: Union Pacific R. Co. v. Locomotive Engineers
description: A case in which the Court further held that pre-arbitration settlement conferences are not a prerequisite for National Railroad Adjustment Board jurisdiction over a dispute.

name: Reed Elsevier v. Muchnick
description: A case in which the Court held that the registration requirement of Section 411(a) of the Copyright Act is a precondition to filing a copyright infringement claim.

name: Salazar v. Buono
description: A case in which the Court held that an individual has standing to maintain a suit when he acquires a "judicially cognizable" interest in ensuring compliance with a previous judgment in his favor. The Court also held that a court may not order an injunction in a case when it fails to consider all the circumstances bearing on the need for preventive relief.

name: Bloate v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that the time granted to prepare pretrial motions is not automatically granted exclusion from the Speedy Trial Act's 70-day time limit.

name: United States v. Stevens
description: A case in which the Court ruled that 18 U.S.C. Section 48 was unconstitutional under the Free Speech Clause of the First Amendment.

name: Johnson v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that the Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals was bound by Florida state law in considering a felony battery charge.

name: Mohawk Industries, Inc. v. Carpenter
description: A case in which the Court held that disclosure orders adverse to attorney-client privilege do not qualify for immediate appeal under the collateral order doctrine.

name: Maryland v. Shatzer
description: A case in which the Court held that the ruling in Edwards v. Arizona does not allow for suppression of statements if a substantial period of time between the invoking one's Miranda rights and a second interrogation takes place.

name: Northwest Austin Municipal Util. Dist. No. One v. Holder
description: A case in which the Court held that the Voting Rights Act (VRA) permits all political subdivisions to seek bailout from the preclearance requirements of the VRA.

name: Forest Grove School District v. T.A.
description: A case in which the Court found that the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) can authorize a public school to reimburse a student for private school tuition sought because the student never received special education services at the public school.

name: Cuomo v. Clearing House Assn., L. L. C.
description: A case in which the Court found that state officials are not precluded from regulating and enforcing banking activities governed by the Office of the Comptroller.

name: Nijhawan v. Holder
description: A case in which the Court found that when an alien is convicted of conspiracy and held responsible for causing more than $10,000 in damages, the statute requirement used by the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) to deport the alien is satisfied, even if the $10,000 is not established by a jury.

name: Bobby v. Bies
description: A case in which the Court found that the Double Jeopardy Clause did not prevent relitigation of a mental retardation claim because the defendant was never acquitted at trial.

name: Ricci v. DeStefano
description: A case in which the Court held that a municipality violated Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 when it rejected otherwise valid civil service exams because the results unintentionally prevented the promotion of minority candidates.

name: United States ex rel. Eisenstein v. City of New York
description: A case in which the Court held that the 30-day limit for filing a claim under the False Claims Act applies when the United States is not a party to the lawsuit.

name: Safford Unified School District v. Redding
description: A case in which the Court held that a school's strip-search to find ibuprofen on a thirteen-year-old girl violated her Fourth Amendment rights.

name: Republic of Iraq v. Beaty
description: Question: Do American courts have jurisdiction over lawsuits filed prior to the revision of 28 U.S.C. Section 1605(a)(7) against the Republic of Iraq when the alleged misdeeds occurred under the regime of Saddam Hussein?

name: Horne v. Flores
description: A case in which the Court found that the lower court incorrectly analyzed Rule 60(b)(5), which allows a party to seek relief from a judgment if a significant change in the law has occurred.

name: Polar Tankers, Inc. v. City of Valdez
description: A case in which the Court held that a property tax which fell exclusively on large vessels and used an apportionment method for out-of-state vessels violated the Tonnage Clause of the Constitution.

name: Gross v. FBL Financial Services, Inc.
description: A case in which the Court held that a plaintiff must show that age was the "but-for" cause for the defendant's action in an Age Discrimination in Employment Act claim.

name: Travelers Indemnity Co. v. Bailey
description: A case in which the Court held that federal bankruptcy courts have jurisdiction to enter orders beyond matters directly related to the execution of a debtor's estate.

name: United States v. Denedo
description: A case in which the Court held that the Navy-Marine Corps Court of Criminal Appeals (NMCCA) retained jurisdiction under the All Writs Act to consider coram nobis petitions that alleged a prior judgment of conviction was fundamentally flawed.

name: Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission
description: A case in which the Court held that corporate funding of independent political broadcasts in elections cannot be limited under the First Amendment.

name: Yeager v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that the Double Jeopardy clause bars retrial if a jury acquits a defendant on some counts but fails to reach a verdict on other counts whose essential elements must have been decided in the defendant's favor.

name: Dean v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that 18 U.S.C. Section 924(c)(1)(A)(iii) does not require proof of intent to discharge a firearm in order to enhance a sentence.

name: Abuelhawa v. United States
description: A case in which the Court found that using a telephone to make a misdemeanor drug purchase does not facilitate the felony of drug distribution.

name: Caperton v. A. T. Massey Coal Co.
description: A case in which the Court held that the Due Process Clause of the 14th Amendment required that a justice recuse himself from a case if one of the parties in the suit donated $3 million to the justice's election campaign.

name: Arthur Andersen LLP v. Carlisle
description: A case in which the Court found that regardless of whether the petitioner is eligible for a stay, a federal court of appeals has jurisdiction over a motion to stay under Section 16(a)(1) of the Federal Arbitration Act.

name: Atlantic Sounding Co., Inc. v. Townsend
description: A case in which the Court held that a seaman may seek punitive damages against his employer if the employer willfully refused to pay maintenance for a seamen's injuries.

name: District Attorney's Office for the Third Judicial District v. Osborne
description: A case in which the Court found that the defendant had no constitutional right to obtain post-conviction access to DNA evidence used against him at trial.

name: Flores-Figueroa v. United States
description: A case in which the Court found that in order to prove aggravated identity theft, the government needs to prove that the defendant knew that the identification he possessed belonged to another person.

name: Hawaii v. Office of Hawaiian Affairs
description: A case in which the Court held that the Apology Resolution did not restrict Hawaii's sovereign authority to transfer publicly held land for private development.

name: Burlington N. & Santa Fe Ry. Co. v. United States
description: A case in which the Court found that the defendants were not liable as the "arranger" for the contamination at issue, and therefore the liability calculations of the district court were appropriate.

name: Carlsbad Tech., Inc. v. HIF Bio, Inc.
description: A case in which the Court held that a district court's declination of supplemental jurisdiction is not a dismissal for which federal appellate review is barred.

name: United States v. Navajo Nation
description: A case in which the Court held that its decision in Navajo I did not terminate the defendant's claim, however, the defendant did not provide sufficient sources of law and therefore the suit should be dismissed.

name: Rivera v. Illinois
description: A case in which the Court found that the Due Process Clause does not require the automatic reversal of a conviction because of the lower court's good-faith error in denying the defendant's pre-trial motion to dismiss a juror.

name: Corley v. United States
description: A case in which the Court found that voluntary confessions made more than six hours after arrest before the person has been presented before judicial officers are inadmissible.

name: Kansas v. Ventris
description: A case in which the Court found that statements obtained for the purpose of impeaching a defendant's testimony, in the absence of a knowing and voluntary waiver of the Sixth Amendment right to counsel, were admissible.

name: Nken v. Holder
description: A case in which the Court held that a court of appeals' decision to stay an alien's removal pending consideration of the alien's petition for review is governed by the 4-factor traditional test.

name: Puckett v. United States
description: A case in which the Court found that the "plain error standard" of Rule 52(b) of the Federal Rules of Criminal Procedure governs if claims forfeited at trial may be raised at the appellate level.

name: Boyle v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that the government need not spell out a connection between criminal enterprises beyond what is apparent in the criminal activity itself.

name: Montejo v. Louisiana
description: A case in which the Court held that after the appointment of an attorney, a defendant does not necessarily need to take additional steps to accept the appointment in order to secure the protections of the Sixth Amendment.

name: Vermont v. Brillon
description: A case in which the Court found that the lower court should not have categorized the defendant's assigned counsel as a state actor, and any delay caused by the assigned counsel should be charged against the defendant and not the state.

name: Knowles v. Mirzayance
description: A case in which the Court found that in order to find counsel ineffective, the defendant must show both "deficient performance" and "prejudice."

name: Coeur Alaska v. S.E. Alaska Conservation Council
description: A case in which the Court held that the United States Army Corps of Engineers had exclusive rights to grant a permit to Coeur Alaska, Inc. to discharge its waste.

name: Harbison v. Bell
description: A case in which the Court held that a certificate of appealability is not required to appeal an order denying a request for federally appointed counsel; and the federally appointed counsel may represent their client in state clemency proceedings and are entitled to compensation for such representation.

name: Ministry of Defense and Support for Armed Forces of Islamic Republic of Iran v. Elahi
description: A case in which the Court held that the defendant's assets in question were not "blocked" under the Terrorism Risk Insurance Act of 2002 and therefore could not be attached to satisfy his judgment against Iran.

name: Ashcroft v. Iqbal
description: A case in which the Court found that high-ranking government officials were not liable for unconstitutional acts by subordinate officials.

name: AT&T Corp. v. Hulteen
description: A case in which the Court held that a company does not violate the Pregnancy Discrimination Act (PDA) or Title VII when it denies retirement benefits to women who took a temporary disability leave while pregnant when the leave was taken before the PDA came into effect.

name: Arizona v. Johnson
description: A case in which the Court held that police may lawfully search an individual during a routine traffic stop if they believe him to be armed and dangerous, even if they had no reason to believe he was involved in criminal activity when he was searched.

name: Cone v. Bell
description: A case in which the Court found that the petitioner was entitled to federal habeas corpus review due to suppression of material evidence, notwithstanding that habeas reviewed had already been presented twice at the state court level.

name: Shinseki v. Sanders
description: A case in which the Court found that the lower court's framework for evaluating VA (Veterans' Affairs) notice errors conflicted with the established law that the Veterans Court "take due account of the rule of the prejudicial error."

name: Pacific Bell Telephone Co. v. LinkLine Communications
description: A case in which the Court held that a "price squeezing" claim cannot be brought under Section 2 of the Sherman Act when the defendant is not under a duty to sell to the plaintiff in the first place.

name: Philip Morris USA Inc. v. Williams
description: A case which the Court dismissed as improvidently granted.

name: Haywood v. Drown
description: A case in which the Court found that prohibiting civil claims against correction officers in their official capacities violated the Supremacy Clause of the Constitution.

name: Fitzgerald v. Barnstable School Committee
description: A case in which the Court found that a claim filed under Title IX for violation of the Equal Protection Clause of the fourteenth Amendment does not preclude the use of 42 U.S.C. Section 1983 which protects against the deprivation of any rights guaranteed by the Constitution and federal law.

name: Entergy Corp. v. Riverkeeper, Inc.
description: A case in which the Court found that the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) was permitted to use a cost-benefit analysis while setting national performance standards for cooling water intake structures.

name: 14 Penn Plaza LLC v. Pyett
description: A case in which the Court held that arbitration clauses in employment contracts are enforceable as a matter of federal law.

name: Kansas v. Colorado
description: A case in which the Court held that expert witness fees should be the same when brought in front of the Supreme Court and the federal district courts.

name: Pleasant Grove City v. Summum
description: A case in which the Court held that a city's refusal to place an organization's monument in a public park is not a violation the organization's First Amendment rights.

name: Bell v. Kelly
description: A case which the Court dismissed regarding whether a court may determine if a defendant suffered from ineffective assistance of counsel when his lawyer failed to introduce witness testimony that may have reduced the defendant's sentence from death to life in prison.

name: Chambers v. United States
description: A case in which the Court found that the "failure to report" crime does not satisfy the Armed Career Criminals Act's (ACCA) "crime of violence" definition.

name: Melendez-Diaz v. Massachusetts
description: A case in which the Court found that a state forensic analyst's lab report prepared for use in a criminal prosecution is subject to the demands of the Sixth Amendment Confrontation Clause.

name: United States v. Hayes
description: Question: Under the Gun Control Act of 1968, does a conviction for misdemeanor battery constitute a "misdemeanor crime of domestic violence" when the victim was the offender's wife and the predicate offense statute did not designate a "domestic relationship" between aggressor and victim as an element of the crime?

name: Negusie v. Holder
description: A case in which the Court held that the Board of Immigration Appeals (BIA) incorrectly interpreted provisions of the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) from a mistaken legal premise.

name: Van de Kamp v. Goldstein
description: A case in which the Court reaffirmed its holding in Imbler, stating that officers of the court (including federal prosecutors) are immune from liability "for actions intimately associated with the judicial phase of the criminal process."

name: FCC v. Fox Television Stations, Inc.
description: A case in which the Court held that the FCC's imposition of liability on Fox Television Stations for fleeting expletives was not "arbitrary and capricious" under the Administrative Procedure Act, even though the FCC previously accepted similar expletives.

name: United States v. Eurodif S.A.
description: A case in which the Court found that the Commerce Department's view of imported low enriched uranium as the sale of goods rather than services was permissible.

name: Jimenez v. Quarterman
description: A case in which the Court held that if a state court grants a criminal defendant the right to file an out-of-time direct appeal, the statute of limitations doesn't begin until after the out-of-time appeal is final.

name: Carcieri v. Salazar
description: A case in which the Court found that only tribes under federal jurisdiction at the time of the Indian Reorganization Act of 1934 are subject to taking by the federal government.

name: Wyeth v. Levine
description: A case in which the Court held that federal law did not preempt state law in a personal injury action against a drug manufacturer for failing to include an appropriate warning label, even where the drug in question met the Food and Drug Administration's (FDA) labeling requirements.

name: Ysursa v. Pocatello Education Association
description: A case in which the Court found that provisions of Idaho's Voluntary Contributions Act which prohibit payroll deductions for "political activities" did not violate the First Amendment when applied to local government employees.

name: Waddington v. Sarausad
description: A case in which the Court found that a federal court may reject a state court's conclusion with respect to the appropriateness of the state court jury instruction, so long as the instructions were "not only erroneous, but objectively unreasonable."

name: Hedgpeth v. Pulido
description: A case in which the Court held that the error of instructing a jury on multiple theories of guilt does not spoil all of the jury's findings, but rather the error should be evaluated by whether it caused a "substantial and injurious effect" on the verdict.

name: Pearson, et al. v. Callahan
description: A case in which the Court overturned its previous decision in Saucier v. Katz, which prescribed a rigid test for government qualified immunity claims, and held that inquiries should be at the discretion of the lower courts.

name: Bartlett v. Strickland
description: A case in which the Court found that the Voting Rights Act of 1965 did not require redistricting in a county lacking a numerical majority of a racial minority of citizens.

name: Oregon v. Ice
description: A case in which the Court found that the Sixth Amendment can assign judges, rather than juries, the responsibility of fact-finding in order to impose consecutive sentences on criminal defendants.

name: Winter v. Natural Resources Defense Council, Inc.
description: A case in which the Court held that the standard for properly granting a preliminary injunction is not based on the "possibility" of irreparable harm to marine life, but rather that "irreparable injury is likely" in the absence of such an injunction.

name: Crawford v. Nashville and Davidson County, TN
description: A case in which the Court held that the anti-retaliation provision of Title VII extends to people who participate in an internal investigation, even if they are not speaking on their own initiative.

name: Summers v. Earth Island Institute
description: A case in which the Court held that the defendants did not have standing to challenge regulations of the U.S. Forest Service in the absence of a live dispute over the application of those regulations.

name: Kennedy v. Plan Administrator for DuPont Sav. and Investment Plan
description: A case in which the Court held that the Employee Retirement Income Security Act's anti-alienation provision nonetheless recognizes a wavier which holds that a spouse's right to the other spouse's pension benefits is void upon divorce.

name: Arizona v. Gant
description: A case in which the Court held that police may search a suspect's vehicle after his arrest only if it is reasonable to believe that the arrestee might access the vehicle at the time of the search or that the vehicle contains evidence of the offense of the arrest.

name: Herring v. United States
description: A case in which the Court found that a criminal defendant's Fourth Amendment rights were not violated when he was unlawfully searched due to isolated negligence of police and not "systematic error or reckless disregard of constitutional requirements."

name: Locke v. Karass
description: A case in which the Court found that fees paid by union nonmembers which were not used to specifically benefit those nonmembers did not violate the First Amendment.

name: Vaden v. Discover Bank
description: A case in which the Court held that a federal court may "look through" a Section 4 petition to determine whether the claim establishes federal subject matter jurisdiction.

name: Altria Group, Inc. v. Good
description: A case in which the Court held that the Federal Cigarette Labeling and Advertising Act did not preempt all claims related to "smoking and health" under the Maine Unfair Trade Practices Act.

name: Meacham v. Knolls Atomic Power Laboratory
description: Question: Under the Supreme Court's decision in Smith v. City of Jackson, must the employer or the employee prove the reasonableness of adverse employment decisions occurring as part of a claim for age discrimination under the federal Age Discrimination in Employment Act?

name: Metropolitan Life Ins. Co. v. Glenn
description: Question: Does an insurance carrier, acting both as the entity determining when awards are to be paid and actually funding those awards, have the right to represent to a court that an individual is disabled when the insurance carrier separately determines for other purposes that the individual is in fact not disabled?

name: Davis v. Federal Election Commission
description: Question: Does the Millionaire's Amendment to the 2002 campaign finance law, which raises the contribution limit for those running against a self-financed candidate, violate free speech clause of the First Amendment and the equal protection principle of the Fifth Amendment?

name: Giles v. California
description: Question: Are a criminal defendant's rights under the Confrontation Clause of the Sixth Amendment violated when the common law "forfeiture by wrongdoing" doctrine is applied to allow out-of-court statements made by a witness, absent due to the defendant's own conduct, into evidence without giving defendant an opportunity to cross-examine the absent witness?

name: Engquist v. Oregon Department of Agriculture
description: Question: Does the Court's ruling in Village of Willowbrook v. Olech, 528 U.S. 562 (2000), allow so-called "class of one" equal protection claims against government bodies in the context of employment discrimination?

name: Sprint Communications Co., L.P. v. APCC Services, Inc.
description: Question: Do third-party companies hired by pay-phone operators to collect compensation for coinless long-distance calls have standing to sue telecommunication companies over the amount of the fees?

name: Kennedy v. Louisiana
description: A case in which the Court held that the Eighth Amendment prevented states from imposing the death penalty for the rape of a child, in which death was not intended nor resulted from the rape.

name: Taylor v. Sturgell
description: Question: Does the dismissal of a claim based on a Freedom of Information Act request preclude a second individual, based on the concept of "virtual representation," from bringing a similar claim when both claims involve the same project and the parties to each suit are represented by the same attorney?

name: Greenlaw v. United States
description: Question: Do federal appellate courts have the authority to hike a criminal defendant's sentence in the absence of a government request to do so?

name: Irizarry v. United States
description: Question: Is a judge required to give both parties advance notice before imposing a criminal sentence that departs from the Federal Sentencing Guidelines?

name: Plains Commerce Bank v. Long Family Land & Cattle Co.
description: Question: Under the U.S. Supreme Court's decisions in Montana v. U.S. _ and _Nevada v. Hicks, do tribal courts have jurisdiction to hear claims based on civil suits against non-members who voluntarily did business with members?

name: Bridge v. Phoenix Bond & Indemnity Co.
description: Question: May individuals and companies bring RICO lawsuits against defendants whose false statements directly harmed them, even if the defendants made these statements to a neutral third party?

name: Florida Department of Revenue v. Piccadilly Cafeterias, Inc.
description: Question: Does 11 U.S.C. Section 1146(c), a provision of the Bankruptcy Code stating that certain asset transfers "under a [confirmed Chapter 11] plan may not be taxed under any law imposing a stamp tax or similar tax," prohibit states from imposing taxes on pre-confirmation asset sales that are essential to the completion of a reorganization plan?

name: Indiana v. Edwards
description: Question: Does the Court's prior ruling that a criminal defendant need only be "literate, competent, and understanding" to represent himself at trial set an appropriate standard for defining that defendant's mental competence to invoke his Sixth Amendment right to self-representation when he is otherwise unable to conduct a coherent defense?

name: United States v. Ressam
description: Question: Does 18 U.S.C. Section 844(h)(2), which prohibits carrying explosives "during the commission of any felony", apply to a defendant convicted of lying to a customs agent because the explosives were not carried "in relation to" the underlying felony?

name: Munaf v. Geren
description: Question: Do U.S. courts have jurisdiction to hear habeas corpus petitions brought on behalf of U.S. citizens detained overseas by American military authorities working as part of a multinational force?

name: United States v. Clintwood Elkhorn Mining Co.
description: Question: Whether the claims of taxpayers seeking refunds for unconstitutionally levied taxes under the Export Clause of the Tucker Act, which applies a six-year statute of limitations, are preempted by the United States Tax Code's three-year statute of limitations for such claims?

name: Burgess v. United States
description: Question: Did the Fourth Circuit err in determining that Burgess' sentencing hike for a drug distribution charge was sufficiently mandated by 21 U.S.C. Section 841(b)(1)(A), which requires such a hike for individuals with prior felony drug convictions regardless of length of imprisonment, when another federal statute, 21 U.S.C. Section 802, requires that a felony drug offense be "punishable by imprisonment for more than a year"?

name: Riley v. Kennedy
description: Question: Under the Voting Rights Act of 1965, was the State of Alabama required to preclear two Alabama Supreme Court decisions invalidating state and local laws creating a special election for local officials in an action against the Governor of Alabama challenging the legality of those elections?

name: Chamber of Commerce of the U.S. v. Brown
description: Question: Does the National Labor Relations Act, which states that companies' anti-labor speech can only be considered unfair labor practice if it threatens or coerces workers, preempt state laws prohibiting the use of state funds to "assist, promote, or deter union organizing," even if the public funds are transparently segregated?

name: Richlin Security Service Co. v. Chertoff
description: Question: Is a plaintiff who has successfully sued the federal government entitled to reimbursement of paralegal fees at market rates or as an expense compensable at cost to the firm under the Equal Access to Justice Act, which allows for recovery of "fees and other expenses" incurred in the proceedings?

name: District of Columbia v. Heller
description: A case in which the Court found a District of Columbia law strictly regulating gun ownership to be unconstitutional.

name: Rothgery v. Gillespie County
description: Question: Did the Fifth Circuit err in holding that Rothgery's right to counsel under the Sixth Amendment was not implicated when he was denied counsel at the time of his initial hearing for being a felon in possession of a firearm but the hearing was conducted without the involvement of a prosecutor?

name: Republic of Philippines v. Pimentel
description: Question: Did the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit err in approving the award of assets to creditors of former Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos when the Philippine government, claiming rightful ownership of the assets, excluded itself from the proceedings based on sovereign immunity?

name: Exxon Shipping Co. v. Baker
description: Question: Does maritime law permit judges to award punitive damages for employee misdeeds and does maritime law allow judge-made remedies when Congress has not authorized them?

name: Allison Engine Co., Inc. v. United States ex rel. Sanders
description: Question: Must whistleblower claimants prove that a private company directly presented a fraudulent bill to the government in order to prevail in a False Claims Act case?

name: Warner-Lambert Co. v. Kent
description: Question: Does a federal law prohibiting fraudulent communications to government agencies preempt a state law permitting plaintiffs to sue for faulty products that would not have reached the market absent the fraud?

name: Regalado Cuellar v. United States
description: Question: Does the federal money laundering statute require the government to prove that the defendant was trying to portray ill-gotten gains as legitimate wealth, or must prosecutors show only that the defendant was attempting to conceal criminal proceeds?

name: CBOCS West, Inc. v. Humphries
description: Question: May a worker sue his employer for retaliation under the Civil Rights Act of 1866?

name: Gómez-Pérez v. Potter
description: Question: Does the ADEA prohibit retaliation against federal employees?

name: Morgan Stanley Capital Group Inc. v. Public Utility District No. 1 of Snohomish County
description: Question: May the government permit utility companies to renegotiate long-term contracts with wholesale energy suppliers and, if so, what circumstances justify renegotiation?

name: MeadWestvaco Corp. v. Illinois Department of Revenue
description: Question: Under the governing Supreme Court precedent, Allied-Signal, Inc. v. Director, Div. of Taxation, 504 U.S. 768 (1992), may a parent company use a division as a non-taxable investment when the division is involved in a substantially different business segment but the parent provides cash infusions, investment advice and oversight?

name: Quanta Computer, Inc., et al. v. LG Electronics, Inc.
description: Question: May a patent holder seek royalties from companies other than its direct purchaser as the patented product is integrated into larger components during the manufacturing process?

name: Begay v. United States
description: Question: Does driving while intoxicated qualify as a violent felony for purposes of the federal career criminal law?

name: United States v. Rodriquez
description: Question: Does a crime qualify as "serious" for purposes of the federal career criminal law when the underlying offense is not considered grave, but carries a high prison sentence because it was not the first?

name: Virginia v. Moore
description: Question: Does the Fourth Amendment require the suppression of evidence obtained incident to an arrest when the arrest violates a provision of state law?

name: Preston v. Ferrer
description: Question: Must a contract dispute to go arbitration pursuant to the document's arbitration clause when an administrative agency has exclusive jurisdiction over the disputed issue?

name: Kentucky Retirement Systems v. EEOC
description: Question: Is the use of age as a factor in a retirement plan "arbitrary" rendering the plan discriminatory on its face in violation of the Age Discrimination in Employment Act?

name: Crawford v. Marion County Election Board
description: Question: Does a law that requires voters to present either a state or federal photo identification unduly burden citizens' right to vote?

name: Boulware v. United States
description: Question: Does the return of capital rule apply automatically when a company without earnings or profits distributes money to a shareholder, or must the taxpayer produce contemporaneous evidence that the money was treated as a return of capital when distributed?

name: Gonzalez v. United States
description: Question: May a magistrate judge conduct voir dire if she has received approval from attorneys for both sides, but has not directly sought or received approval from the defendant?

name: Baze v. Rees
description: Question: Is the use of a four-drug lethal injection process to carry out death sentences a violation of the Eighth Amendment ban on cruel and unusual punishment?

name: Dada v. Mukasey
description: Question: When an illegal resident agrees to voluntarily depart the United States and then files a motion to reopen removal proceedings, does the filing suspend the time period by which the illegal resident must depart the United States under the voluntary departure order?

name: Boumediene v. Bush
description: A case in which the Court held that the Military Commissions Act of 2006 violated the Suspension Clause of the Constitution.

name: Riegel v. Medtronic, Inc.
description: Question: Does Section 360k(a) of the Medical Device Amendments to the Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act preempt state-law claims seeking damages for injuries caused by medical devices that received premarket approval from the Food and Drug Administration.

name: Snyder v. Louisiana
description: Question: Did the state's dismissal by peremptory challenge of all of the black potential jurors, combined with the prosecution's comparisons of the case to the O.J. Simpson trial, amount to a violation of the Equal Protection Clause?

name: Sprint/United Management Co. v. Mendelsohn
description: Question: In employment discrimination cases, must a court admit "me, too" evidence - testimony by other employees who are not parties to the case and who were allegedly discriminated against by persons who had no role in the employment decision being challenged by the plaintiff?

name: Rowe v. New Hampshire Motor Transport Association
description: Question: Does the Federal Aviation Administration Authorization Act of 1994 preempt a state law that uses the state's police power to require that air and motor carriers take steps to ensure that tobacco is not sold to minors?

name: Knight v. Commissioner of Internal Revenue
description: Question: Does 26 U.S.C. 67(e) allow trusts and estates to fully deduct the cost of investment management and advisory services on their income tax returns?

name: New Jersey v. Delaware
description: Question: Does Delaware, under a 1905 compact with New Jersey settling boundary disputes, have the right to refuse to grant a permit for a construction project occurring mainly on New Jersey land but involving underwater land within Delaware's coastal zone?

name: LaRue v. DeWolff, Boberg & Associates, Inc.
description:
Question:
  1. Does Section 502(a)(2) of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 allow an employee pension plan participant to sue the plan manager for losses caused by breach of fiduciary duties in administering the plan, even when the losses affected only the participant's personal account?
  2. Does a suit brought by a plan participant against the plan manager for breach of fiduciary duty qualify as a suit for "equitable relief" for the purposes of Section 502(a)(3) of ERISA?

name: Hall Street Associates, L.L.C. v. Mattel, Inc.
description: Question: Can a federal court enforce an arbitration agreement that provides for more expansive judicial review of an arbitration award than the narrow standard of review provided for in the Federal Arbitration Act?

name: Federal Express Corporation v. Holowecki
description: Question: Does an intake questionnaire submitted to the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission qualify as the charge of discrimination required by the Age Discrimination in Employment Act, even if the EEOC did not treat the questionnaire as a charge?

name: John R. Sand & Gravel Company v. United States
description: Question: Is the six-year statute of limitations in the Tucker Act a jurisdictional requirement?

name: CSX Transportation, Inc. v. Georgia State Board of Equalization
description: Question: Does the Railroad Revitalization and Regulatory Reform Act of 1976 require a federal district court determining the "true market value" of railroad property to accept the valuation method chosen by the State?

name: Department of Revenue of Kentucky v. Davis
description: Question: Does a state violate the dormant Commerce Clause by providing an income tax exemption for interest on bonds issued by the state, while denying the exemption to interest on bonds issued by other states?

name: Danforth v. Minnesota
description: Question: When determining whether Supreme Court decisions on constitutional rules of criminal procedure apply retroactively, may state supreme courts use state-law retroactivity standards that are broader than the standard in Teague v. Lane?

name: Logan v. United States
description: Question: Are convictions that do not result in loss of civil rights excluded from the three convictions necessary to activate the Armed Career Criminal Act's sentence enhancement?

name: United States v. Williams
description: Question: Does the PROTECT Act abridge First Amendment freedom of speech by outlawing the pandering of material that is believed to be, or claimed to be, illegal child pornography?

name: Ali v. Federal Bureau of Prisons
description: Question: In the detention of goods exception to the waiver of sovereign immunity in the Federal Tort Claims Act, is the phrase "other law enforcement officer" limited to officers acting in a tax, excise, or customs capacity?

name: Klein & Co. Futures, Inc. v. Board of Trade of the City of New York
description: Question: Do futures commission merchants, who buy and sell futures contracts on behalf of others, "engage[] in [...] transaction[s]" subject to the rules of a commodity board of trade and therefore have standing to sue under Section 22 of the Commodities Exchange Act?

name: Medellin v. Texas
description:
Question:
  1. Did the President act within his constitutional and statutory foreign affairs authority when he determined that states must comply with the U.S. treaty obligation under the Vienna Convention by enforcing a decision of the International Court of Justice?
  2. Does the Constitution require state courts to honor the treaty obligation of the U.S. by enforcing a decision of the International Court of Justice?

name: Stoneridge Investment Partners, LLC v. Scientific-Atlanta, Inc.
