description: Question: May a State, consistent with the Due Process and Equal Protection Clauses of the Fourteenth Amendment, condition appeals from trial court decrees terminating parental rights on the affected parent's ability to pay record preparation fees?

name: Felker v. Turpin
description: Question: Do the Act's Title I provisions, preventing the Supreme Court from reviewing an appellate review panel's denial of leave to file a second habeas petition, unconstitutionally "suspend" the habeas writ and restrict the Court's authority to entertain original habeas petitions?

name: United States v. Winstar Corporation
description: Question: Can the federal government be sued by thrifts that were sent into financial trouble when Congress changed the computation of required reserves after the Federal Home Loan Bank Board encouraged actions based on premise that the rules would not change?

name: Smiley v. Citibank (South Dakota), N. A.
description: Question: Does the National Bank Act of 1864 authorize a national bank to charge late-payment fees that are lawful in the bank's home State but prohibited in the States where the cardholders reside?

name: Lewis v. United States
description: Question: Does a defendant who is prosecuted in a single proceeding for multiple petty offenses have a constitutional right to a jury trial where the aggregate prison term authorized for the offenses exceeds six months? May a defendant who would otherwise have a constitutional right to a jury trial be denied that right because the presiding judge has made a pretrial commitment that the aggregate sentence imposed will not exceed six months?

name: Medtronic Inc. v. Lohr
description: Question: Do the Medical Device Amendments of 1976 pre-empt a state common-law negligence action against the manufacturer of an allegedly defective medical device?

name: Lockheed Corporation v. Spink
description: Question: May a business offer early retirement benefits on the condition that an employee give up the right to sue over any job-related claim? Can the federal government retroactively apply retirement income benefit laws?

name: Auciello Iron Works, Inc. v. National Labor Relations Board
description: Question: May an employer disavow a collective-bargaining agreement because of a good-faith doubt about a union's majority status at the time the contract was made, when the doubt arises from facts known to the employer before its contract offer had been accepted by the union?

name: Degen v. United States
description: Question: Should the fugitive disentitlement doctrine be extended to allow a court in a civil forfeiture suit to enter judgment against a claimant, without any opportunity to be heard, because the claimant is a fugitive from, or otherwise is resisting, a related criminal prosecution?

name: United States v. Ursery
description: Question: Do civil property forfeitures ("in rem" forfeiture) constitute a "punishment" in terms of the Fifth Amendment's double jeopardy clause which forbids successive prosecutions and punishment for the same crime?

name: Whren v. United States
description: Question: Did the officers conduct an unreasonable search and seizure in violation of the Fourth Amendment?

name: Doctor's Associates Inc. v. Casarotto
description: Question: Does the Federal Arbitration Act preempt Montana's first-page notice of arbitration requirement?

name: Gasperini v. Center for Humanities Inc.
description: Question: Does New York's law that empowers appellate courts to review the size of jury's awards conflict with the Seventh Amendment's guarantee of jury trials in civil cases?

name: Lane v. Peña
description: Question: Did Congress waive the federal government's sovereign immunity against monetary damages with respect to section 504(a) of the 1973 Rehabilitation Act?

name: Gray v. Netherland
description: Question: Can a defendant sentenced to death argue in his habeas corpus petition that prosecutors deceived him, in violation of the Fourteenth Amendment Due Process Clause, by producing surprise evidence in the sentencing phase of the trial?

name: Colorado Republican Federal Campaign Committee v. Federal Election Commission
description: Question: Do the federal campaign-financing limits on the amount of money political parties may spend on congressional races, as established by the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971, violate First Amendment rights when applied to expenditures a political party has made independently of any candidate's campaign?

name: Brown v. Pro Football Inc.
description: Question: Are several employers immune from a union anti-trust suit when these employers, bargaining together, unilaterally impose terms on the union if the collective bargaining process reaches an impasse?

name: Ornelas v. United States
description: Question: Should courts use a de novo standard in determining if a police search conducted without a warrant was based on reasonable suspicion and probable cause?

name: Richards  v. Jefferson County
description: Question: May the Alabama residents, who claim that the Jefferson County occupation tax violates the Federal and Alabama Constitutions, proceed with their class action suit in court in light of a prior, similar adjudication?

name: United States  v. Noland
description: Question: May a bankruptcy court subordinate government attempts to collect tax penalties?

name: United States v. Reorganized CF&I Fabricators of Utah, Inc.
description: Question: Is the Internal Revenue Code's 10% tax liability claim on any "accumulated funding deficiency" in pension plans an "excise tax" under the Bankruptcy Code? May the Government's tax claims be given a lower priority than competing claims by other creditors in bankruptcy proceedings?

name: Montana v. Egelhoff
description: Question: May a state restrict the elements of a defense in criminal prosecution, consistent with the Fourteenth Amendment Due Process Clause?

name: O'Hare Truck Service, Inc. v. City of Northlake
description: Question: Did O'Hare Truck Service's removal from Northlake's employment list, as a result of its support for an opposition mayoral candidate, violate O'Hare Truck Services freedom of speech?

name: Henderson v. United States
description: Question: Is service of process under the Suits of Admiralty Act a matter of procedure governed by the uniform Federal Rules of Civil Procedure?

name: Exxon Company, U.S.A. v. Sorec, Inc.
description: Question: Does the "superseding cause" doctrine apply to admiralty cases in which the court previously has adopted a comparative fault principle?

name: United States v. International Business Machines Corporation
description: Question: May the federal government impose a tax on premiums that U.S. businesses pay foreign insurers for risks that could arise in this country?

name: O'Connor v. Consolidated Coin Caterers Corporation
description: Question: Can an employee file an age discrimination suit under the Age Discrimination in Employment Act of 1967 if his or her replacement is 40 or older?

name: Melendez v. United States
description: Question: Does a federal prosecutor's plea agreement that a cooperating defendant be given the minimum sentence authorize a judge to depart below a statutory minimum?

name: Jaffee v. Redmond
description: Question: Can psychotherapists be forced to provide evidence about their patients in federal court cases?

name: United States v. Armstrong
description: Question: Must criminal defendants who pursue selective-prosecution claims demonstrate people of other races were not prosecuted for similar crimes?

name: Holly Farms Corporation v. National Labor Relations Board
description: Question: Did the National Labor Relations Board correctly classify chicken catchers as employees, and not as exempt agricultural workers, for purposes of the National Labor Relations Act?

name: Denver Area Educational Telecommunications Consortium, Inc. v. Federal Communications Commission
description: Question: Do the Television Consumer Protection and Competition Act's empowerments and restrictions violate the petitioner's First Amendment right to freedom of speech?

name: United Food & Commercial Workers v. Brown Group, Inc.
description: Question: May a labor union sue on behalf of its members over alleged violations of the federal Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act?

name: Koon v. United States
description: Question: Did the Court of Appeals use the wrong standard in deciding whether a federal trial judge had erred in departing from the federal Sentencing Guidelines and giving lighter sentences to two ex-policemen convicted in the beating of Rodney King?

name: Quackenbush v. Allstate Insurance Company
description: Question: Is an abstention-based remand order appealable as a final order? Can the abstention doctrine recognized in Burford v. Sun Oil Co. be applied in a suit for damages?

name: United States v. Virginia
description: A case in which the Court found that the Virginia Military Institute's policy of only admitting and serving males was unconstitutional.

name: Cooper v. Oklahoma
description: Question: May state law presume that defendants are competent to stand trial unless they prove their incompetence by clear and convincing evidence without violating the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment?

name: Carlisle v. United States
description: Question: Does a district court have the authority to grant a post-verdict motion for judgment of acquittal if the motion is filed beyond the seven-day deadline prescribed by Federal Rule of Criminal Procedure 29(c)?

name: Barnett Bank of Marion County, N.A. v. Nelson
Wisconsin v. City of New York
description: Question: Did the decision of the Secretary of Commerce not to use the PES in the 1990 census violate the constitutional right of certain minorities to be counted?

name: Meghrig v. KFC Western, Inc.
description: Question: May plaintiffs use the federal Resource Conservation and Recovery Act of 1976 to sue and recover money they spent to clean up hazardous waste on their property?

name: Loving v. United States
description: Question: Does the President have the authority, consistent with the separation-of-powers principle, to prescribe aggravating factors that permit a court-martial to impose the death penalty upon a member of the armed forces convicted of murder?

name: Lotus Development Corporation v. Borland International, Inc.
description: Question: Is a computer program's menu command hierarchy a "method of operation" under 17 U.S.C.102(b), and therefore uncopyrightable?

name: Norfolk & Western Railway Company v. Hiles
description: Question: Is a railroad liable, under the federal Safety Appliance Act, for injuries incurred by a railroad employee while trying to straighten a misaligned drawbar?

name: Markman v. Westview Instruments, Inc.
description: Question: Is the interpretation of a patent's claim, the portion of the patent document that defines the scope of the patentee's rights, a matter of fact to be decided by jurors?

name: United States v. Chesapeake & Potomac Telephone Co. of Va.
description: Question: Does 47 U.S.C. 533(b), which bars local telephone companies from directly providing video programming to their local phone service subscribers, violate the First Amendment's protection of free speech?

name: Shaw v. Hunt
description: Question: Does North Carolina's redistricting plan constitute racial gerrymandering in violation of the Fourteenth Amendment's equal protection clause?

name: Bush v. Vera
description: Question: Do the Texas redistricting plans violate the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment?

name: Neal v. United States
description: Question: Does U.S. Sentencing Commission's Guidelines Manual's revised system for determining LSD amounts take precedence over 21 U.S.C. 841 in determining sentencing?

name: Lonchar v. Thomas
description: Question: May a federal court dismiss a first federal habeas petition for general "equitable" reasons beyond those embodied in the federal Habeas Corpus Rules?

name: Lewis v. Casey
description: Question: Did a federal trial judge err when ruling that Arizona prison officials unconstitutionally failed to provide inmates with adequate legal research facilities?

name: Bennis v. Michigan
description: Question: Does the abatement order entered against Bennis's car constitute a taking of private property for public use in violation of the property clauses of the Fifth and Fourteenth Amendments?

name: Board of County Commissioners, Wabaunsee County, Kansas v. Umbehr
description: Question: Did the Board's termination of Umbehr's contract, presumably as a result of his criticisms, constitute a violation of his First Amendment freedom of speech?

name: Bank One Chicago, N.A. v. Midwest Bank & Trust Company
description: Question: Does the Expedited Funds Availability Act provide for federal-court jurisdiction only in suits between customers and banks?

name: Rutledge v. United States
description: Question: Can a criminal be given concurrent life sentences for conspiring to distribute drugs and operating a continuing criminal enterprise?

name: Matsushita Elec. Industrial Company v. Epstein
description: Question: May a federal court refuse to grant full faith and credit to a state-court judgment approving a class-action settlement simply because the settlement releases claims within the exclusive jurisdiction of the federal courts?

name: Zicherman v. Korean Air Lines Company
description: Question: May a plaintiff, in a suit brought under Article 17 of the Warsaw Convention governing international air transportation, recover damages for loss of society resulting from the death of a relative in a plane crash on the high seas?

name: Behrens v. Pelletier
description: Question: Does a defendant's immediate appeal of an unfavorable qualified-immunity ruling on his motion to dismiss deprive the court of appeals of jurisdiction over a second appeal, also based on qualified immunity, immediately following denial of summary judgment?

name: Peacock v. Thomas
description: Question: Do federal courts possess ancillary jurisdiction over new actions in which a federal judgment creditor seeks to impose liability for a money judgment on a person not otherwise liable for the judgment?

name: Commissioner v. Lundy
description: Question: Can the Tax Court award a refund of taxes paid more than two years prior to the date on which the Commissioner of Internal Revenue mailed the taxpayer a notice of deficiency, when, on the date the notice of deficiency was mailed, the taxpayer had not yet filed a return?

name: 44 Liquormart Inc. v. Rhode Island
description: Question: Is Rhode Island's statute an infringement on the First Amendment right to commercial freedom of speech? If it is, can Rhode Island still pass such legislation under the Twenty-first Amendment which limits the dormant Commerce Clause by empowering the states to regulate the sale of alcohol?

name: Varity Corporation v. Howe
description: Question: Did the Varity Corporation and Massey-Ferguson, Inc. act their capacity as an Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974fiduciary when they significantly and deliberately misled the beneficiaries? By doing so, did Varity and Massey-Ferguson violate the fiduciary obligations that ERISA imposes upon plan administrators? Does ERISA authorize a lawsuit in such cases?

name: Fulton Corporation v. Faulkner
description: Question: Does North Carolina's "intangibles tax" on a fraction of the value of corporate stock owned by North Carolina residents inversely proportional to the corporation's exposure to the State's income tax violate the Federal Commerce Clause?

name: Yamaha Motor Corporation, U.S.A. v. Calhoun
description: Question: Do state remedies apply in maritime wrongful-death cases in which no federal statute specifies the appropriate relief and the decedent was not a seaman, longshore worker, or person otherwise engaged in a maritime trade?

name: Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers v. Atchison, Topeka & Santa Fe Railroad Company
Hercules Inc. v. United States
description: Question: May the chemical manufacturers of Agent Orange recover costs incurred from defending and settling third-party tort claims arising out of their performance of Government contracts from the Government on alternative theories of contractual indemnification or warranty of specifications provided by the Government?

name: Robinson v. United States
description: Question: Is evidence of the proximity and accessibility of a firearm to drugs or drug proceeds alone sufficient to support a conviction for "use" of a firearm during and in relation to a predicate narcotics offense under 18 U.S.C. Section 924(c)(1)?

name: BMW of North America, Inc. v. Gore
description: Question: Assuming that Gore's punitive damage award was grossly excessive, does the Fourteenth Amendment's due process clause protect BMW from paying the award?

name: Seminole Tribe of Florida v. Florida
description: Question: Does the Eleventh Amendment provide Florida with immunity from the Tribe lawsuit?

name: National Labor Relations Board v. Town & Country Electric, Inc.
description: Question: Does a worker qualify as an "employee" under the National Labor Relations Act if, while he is working, he is simultaneously paid by a union to help the union organize a company?

name: Romer v. Evans
description: A case in which the Court found a Colorado amendment that banned protection from discrimination based on sexual orientation violated the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.

name: Citizens Bank of Maryland v. Strumpf
Things Remembered, Inc. v. Petrarca
description: Question: May a federal court of appeals review a district court order remanding a bankruptcy case to state court on grounds of untimely removal?

name: Morse v. Republican Party of Virginia
description: Question: Does section 5 of the Voting Rights Act of 1965 require preclearance of the Republican Party of Virginia's decision to exact a fee to nominate the party's candidate for senator? Are voters permitted to challenge the fee as a poll tax prohibited by section 10?

name: Capitol Square Review and Advisory Bd. v. Pinette
description: Question: Did the Board's denial of a permit to the Ku Klux Klan violate free speech under the First Amendment?

name: Metropolitan Stevedore Company v. Rambo
description: Question: Does the Longshore and Harbor Workers' Compensation Act allow a party to seek modification of a disability award on the ground of change in conditions, when there has been no change in the employee's physical condition but rather an increase in the employee's wage-earning capacity due to the acquisition of new skills?

name: Hurley v. Irish-American Gay, Lesbian and Bisexual Group of Boston, Inc.
description: Question: Did a Massachusetts State Court's mandate to Boston's Veterans' Council, requiring it to include GLIB members in its parade, violate the Council's free speech rights as protected by the First and Fourteenth Amendments?

name: North Star Steel Company v. Thomas
description: Question: Is state law the proper source of the limitations period for civil actions brought to enforce the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act?

name: Oklahoma Tax Commission v. Chickasaw Nation
Milwaukee v. Cement Div., National Gypsum Co.
description: Question: Does the fact that a plaintiff's loss was primarily attributable to its own negligence, together with the existence of a genuine dispute over liability, justify a District Court's departure from the general rule that prejudgment interest should be awarded in maritime collision cases?

name: Miller v. Johnson
description: Question: Is racial gerrymandering of the congressional redistricting process a violation of the Equal Protection Clause?

name: Ryder v. United States
description: Question: Is it proper to accord de facto validity to the actions of civilian judges on a military appellate panel, when the accused challenges the composition of the panel as a violation of the Constitution's Appointments Clause?

name: National Private Truck Council, Inc. v. Oklahoma Tax Commission
Johnson v. Jones
description: Question: Is a Federal District Court's determination, in denying a summary judgment motion of police officers entitled to assert a qualified immunity defense, that the record raised a factual issue an appealable final decision?

name: Babbitt v. Sweet Home Chapter, Communities for a Great Oregon
description: Question: Does the definition of "harm" as an expansion of the word "take" in the Endangered Species Act include habitat modification that kills or injures wildlife?

name: Wilson v. Arkansas
description: Question: Does the Fourth Amendment's reasonable search and seizure clause require police officers to knock and announce their presence before entering a private residence?

name: Vernonia School District 47J v. Acton
description: A case in which the Court held that an Oregon public school did not violate students' Fourth Amendment rights by mandating random drug tests for student athletes.

name: Wilton v. Seven Falls Company
description: Question: Does the exceptional circumstances test govern a district court's decision to stay a declaratory judgment action during the pendency of parallel state court proceedings? Should a court of appeals evaluate a district court's decision to do so under an abuse of discretion standard of review?

name: First Options of Chicago, Inc. v. Kaplan
description: Question: Is the arbitrability of disputes subject to independent review by the courts? Should courts of appeals apply an "abuse of discretion" standard when reviewing district court upholding arbitration awards?

name: United States v. Aguilar
description:
Question: (1) Can an individual who endeavors to obstruct a grand jury proceeding by making false and misleading statements to prospective witnesses be prosecuted for obstruction of justice?
(2) Can an individual who knows of a wiretap and discloses it to a target in order to obstruct the interception of the target's conversations be found guilty, regardless of whether the authorization had expired by the time the disclosure was made?

name: Vimar Seguros y Reaseguros, S. A. v. M/V Sky Reefer
Rosenberger v. Rector and Visitors of the University of Virginia
description: Question: Did the University of Virginia violate the First Amendment rights of its Christian magazine staff by denying them the same funding resources that it made available to secular student-run magazines?

name: City of Edmonds v. Oxford House, Inc.
description: Question: Does the City of Edmonds' zoning code provision covering areas zoned for single-family dwelling units -- which defines family as persons related by genetics, adoption, or marriage, or a group of five or fewer unrelated persons -- qualify for exemption from the Fair Housing Act?

name: Shalala v. Whitecotton
description: Question: Must a claimant seeking compensation under the National Childhood Vaccine Injury Act show that the first symptom of an injury began after receiving the vaccination?

name: Reynoldsville Casket Company v. Hyde
description: Question: Can Ohio apply its unconstitutional tolling provision to claims that accrued prior to Bendix?

name: New York State Conference of Blue Cross & Blue Shield Plans v. Travelers Ins. Co.
Adarand Constructors, Inc. v. Peña
description: A case in which the Court found that in order to uphold the Fifth Amendment, strict scrutiny must be applied if race is the sole indicator of disadvantage.

name: Florida Bar v. Went For It Inc.
description: Question: Do the Florida Bar rules prohibiting direct mail solicitation of accident victims violate the free speech of personal injury attorneys?

name: Mastrobuono v. Shearson Lehman Hutton, Inc.
California Dept. of Corrections v. Morales
Qualitex Company v. Jacobson Products Company, Inc.
Director, Office of Workers' Compensation Programs v. Newport News Shipbuilding & Drydock Company
Arizona v. Evans
description: Question: Does the exclusionary rule prohibit the introduction of the evidence seized in violation of the Fourth Amendment on the basis of an erroneous police record?

name: Nationsbank of North Carolina, N.A. v. Variable Annuity Life Insurance Company
Milwaukee Brewery Workers' Pension Plan v. Jos. Schlitz Brewing Company
Rubin v. Coors Brewing Company
description: a case in which the Court held that for the government to regulate commercial speech, the government must have a substantial interest that the regulation directly affects.

name: Plaut v. Spendthrift Farm, Inc.
description: Question: Did Congress violate separation of powers by requiring federal courts reopen settled cases as part of the FDIC Improvement Act?

name: U. S. Term Limits, Inc. v. Thornton
description: Question: Can states alter those qualifications for the U.S. Congress that are specifically enumerated in the Constitution?

name: Oklahoma Tax Commission v. Jefferson Lines, Inc.
Stone v. Immigration and Naturalization Service
United States v. National Treasury Employees Union
description: Question: Does the honoraria ban abridge freedom of speech as protected by the First Amendment?

name: United States v. Lopez
description: A case in which the Court found the 1990 Gun-Free School Zones Act unconstitutional for overstepping the congressional boundaries of the Commerce Clause.

name: Asgrow Seed Company v. Winterboer
description: Question: Is the quantity of protected seed that a farmer can sell under the exemptions in the Plant Variety Protection Act limited to the amount of seed the seller would need to replant his own fields?

name: Lebron v. National Railroad Passenger Corporation
Kyles v. Whitley
description:
Question: (1) Would the prosecution’s production of evidence favorable to Kyles have resulted in acquittal or mistrial?
(2) Would the prosecution’s production of evidence favorable to Kyles have created sufficient doubt in the mind of at least one juror to result in a life sentence rather than the death penalty?

name: McKennon v. Nashville Banner Publishing Co.
American Airlines, Inc. v. Wolens
description: Question: Does the Airline Deregulation Act of 1978 preempt a state-court suit, brought by participants in an airline's frequent flyer program, challenging the airline's retroactive changes in terms and conditions of the program?

name: Interstate Commerce Commission v. Transcon Lines
Brown v. Gardner
description: Question: Is Department of Veterans Affairs regulation 38 CFR 3.358 (c)(3), which restricts disability compensation to injuries caused by accidents or negligence during surgery, consistent with the controlling statute, 38 U.S.C. 1151?

name: Jerome B. Grubart, Inc. v. Great Lakes Dredge & Dock Company
description: A case in which the Court held that a federal district court had federal admiralty jurisdiction to determine and limit the extent of the Great Lakes Dredge and Dock Company’s tort liability.

name: McIntyre v. Ohio Elections Commission
description: Question: Does the prohibition of the distribution of anonymous campaign literature abridge freedom of speech as protected by the First and Fourteenth Amendments?

name: Nebraska Department of Revenue v. Loewenstein
Federal Election Commission v. NRA Political Victory Fund
United States v. X-Citement Video, Inc.
description: Question: Did the Act's use of the term "knowingly" violate the First Amendment's Free Speech clause by not mandating a showing that the alleged offender knew which materials contained under-age performances?

name: Tome v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that Rule 801(d)(1)(B) requires that prior consistent statements be made before the motive to fabricate arose in order to be admissible.

name: Allied-Bruce Terminix Co. v. Dobson
description: Question: Should the Federal Arbitration Act, making an arbitration provision enforceable in contracts "evidencing a transaction involving commerce," be applied broadly?

name: U.S. Bancorp Mortgage Company v. Bonner Mall Partnership
Hess v. Port Authority Trans-Hudson Corporation
Madsen v. Women's Health Center, Inc.
description: Question: 1) Is the prohibition of all protesting within the 36-foot buffer zone around the front of the clinic an infringement of the First Amendment right to free speech? 2) Is the 36-foot buffer zone along the back and side of the clinic a breach of the First Amendment right to free speech? 3) Do the limitations imposed on noise-making constitute a breach of the First Amendment right to free speech? 4) Do the restrictions placed on the use of images violate the First Amendment right to free speech? 5) Is it a breach of the First Amendment right to free speech to bar protesters from approaching potential patients when they are within a 300-foot radius of the clinic? 6) Is it a violation of the First Amendment right to free speech to prohibit all protesting in a 300-foot radius of clinic staff residences?

name: Morgan Stanley & Co. v. Pacific Mut. Life Ins. Co.
Director, Office of Workers' Compensation Programs v. Greenwich Collieries
Howlett v. Birkdale Shipping Company, S.A.
Honda Motor Company, Ltd. v. Oberg
description: Question: Does the Oregon prohibition on judicial review of jury awards violate the Due Process Clause of the 14th Amendment?

name: Ibanez v. Florida Dept. of Business and Professional Regulation, Bd. of Accountancy
description: Question: Does the Board's decision to censure Ibanez use of her CPA and CFP designations violate the freedom of speech protected by the First Amendment?

name: Heck v. Humphrey
description:
Question: (1) Can a state prisoner attacking the legality of his conviction circumvent the habeas corpus exhaustion requirement by filing an action under 42 U.S.C. § 1983 and confining his prayer for relief to a declaratory judgment and money damages?
(2) Should a state prisoner's action attacking the legality of his conviction that includes unexhausted claims be dismissed without prejudice?

name: Board of Education of Kiryas Joel Village School District v. Grumet
description: Question: Did the 1989 statute violate the First Amendment's Establishment?

name: Stansbury v. California
description: Question: May a trial court determine that a criminal defendant is not "in custody" for Miranda purposes on the basis of police officers' subjective and undisclosed conclusions that they did not consider the defendant a "suspect"?

name: Davis v. United States
description: Question: When a suspect makes an ambiguous request for counsel during a custodial interrogation, must the interrogator cease questioning until the suspect is provided with counsel?

name: Key Tronic Corporation v. United States
Associated Industries of Missouri v. Lohman
description: Question: Does Missouri's use tax violate the Commerce Clause by discriminating against interstate commerce in those localities where the use tax exceeds the local sales tax?

name: Barclay's Bank, PLC v. Franchise Tax Bd. of California
description:
Question: 1) Does a state violate the Due Process Clause by accepting "reasonable approximations" of financial data?
2) By requiring multinational corporations to provide exhaustive financial information to calculate taxes, does a State impose a disproportionately large compliance burden upon the corporation and thereby violate the anti-discrimination requirement of the Commerce Clause?

name: Department of Taxation and Finance of N. Y. v. Milhelm Attea & Bros.
O'Melveny & Myers v. Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation
Beecham v. United States
description: Question: Under 18 U.S.C. 922(g), can state procedures for the restoration of the civil rights of felons restore the right of a federal felon to possess a firearm?

name: MCI Telecommunications Corporation v. American Telephone & Telegraph Company
West Lynn Creamery, Inc. v. Healy
description: Question: Is the Massachusetts pricing order a breach of the Commerce Clause?

name: United States v. Alvarez-Sanchez
description: Question: Does federal statute 18 U.S.C. Section 3501(c), declaring separate charge-based confessions inadmissible if obtained after the first six hours of detention, apply to suspects that are held only on state or federal charges?

name: Kokkonen v. Guardian Life Insurance Company of America
Ticor Title Insurance Company v. Brown
Consolidated Rail Corporation v. Gottshall
description: Question: Under the Federal Employers' Liability Act (FELA), does "emotional stress" resulting from employer "negligence" constitute an "injury" for which an employee can hold his employer liable?

name: Security Services, Inc. v. Kmart Corporation
PUD No. 1 of Jefferson County v. Washington Department of Ecology
City of Ladue v. Gilleo
description: Question: Does the Ladue ordinance violate Gilleo's right to free speech as protected by the First Amendment?

name: National Labor Relations Board v. Health Care Corporation of America
Digital Equipment Corporation v. Desktop Direct, Inc.
description: Question: Is the denial of a "right not to sue" established by a settlement agreement immediately appealable under the Supreme Court's decision in Coopers & Lybrand v. Livesay, 437 U.S. 463?

name: City of Chicago v. Environmental Defense Fund
Department of Revenue of Montana v. Kurth Ranch
Oregon Waste Systems, Inc. v. Oregon Department of Environmental Quality
description: Question: Is the surcharge that Oregon imposed on the in-state disposal of waste produced out-of-state a violation of the Commerce Clause?

name: Simmons v. South Carolina
description: A case in which the Court held that a state court’s refusal to instruct a jury in a sentencing trial that a defendant is ineligible for parole violated the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.

name: Farmer v. Brennan
description: Question: Is Farmer entitled to damages or an injunction against various federal prison officials responsible for transferring her to, or assigning Farmer within, a prison facility where Farmer was sexually assaulted by another inmate?

name: Turner Broadcasting System, Inc. v. Federal Communications Commission
description: Question: Are the must-carry rules content-based and thus a violation of the cable companies' First Amendment right to free speech?

name: McDermott, Inc. v. AmClyde & River Don Castings
Boca Grande Club, Inc. v. Florida Power & Light Co.
United States v. Granderson
description: Question: United States Code section 3565 says that if a person serving a sentence of probation possesses illegal drugs, "the court shall revoke the sentence of probation and sentence the defendant to not less than one third of the original sentence." Does "original sentence" refer to the original imprisonment sentence range set by U.S. Sentencing Guidelines, or to the term of probation?

name: National Organization for Women, Inc. v. Scheidler
description: Question: Does RICO require that an organization, to be defined as a racketeering enterprise, must be acting in pursuit of an economic motive?

name: Fogerty v. Fantasy, Inc.
description: Question: Do federal courts have discretion over whether or not to force a losing party to pay all or part of the victorious party's attorney's fees?

name: C & A Carbone, Inc. v. Town of Clarkstown
description: Question: Does a town's "flow control ordinance," which requires that all waste pass through a certain waste processing plant, violate the interstate Commerce Clause by disrupting commerce for waste processing plants in other states?

name: BFP v. Resolution Trust Corporation
description: Question: Does a property's fair market value determine whether the amount of debt settled by a foreclosure sale is "reasonably equivalent" to the property's worth, as required by U.S.C. Section 548(a)(2)(A)?

name: ABF Freight Systems, Inc. v. National Labor Relations Board
description: Question: Can the National Labor Relations Board grant reinstatement with backpay to an employee who lied under oath during his administrative hearing?

name: Waters v. Churchill
description: Question: Was Churchill's firing impermissible under the First Amendment?

name: Central Bank of Denver , N. A. v. First Interstate Bank of Denver , N. A.
description: Question: Does the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 impose a private liability for aiding and abetting manipulative or deceptive trading practices?

name: Northwest Airlines, Inc. v. County of Kent
International Union, United Mine Workers of America v. Bagwell
description: Question: Were the fines assessed against the United Mine Workers of America union, amounting to more than $64 million, criminal or civil in nature?

name: Campbell v. Acuff-Rose Music, Inc.
description: Question: May 2 Live Crew's commercial parody of Roy Orbison's "Oh, Pretty Woman" be a fair use within the meaning of the Copyright Act of 1976?

name: American Dredging Company v. Miller
description: Question: Does the Constitutional grant of federal jurisdiction over maritime law (found in Article III Section 2) prevent states from prohibiting (in maritime cases) "forum non conveniens" claims that, under federal law, would be permitted?

name: United States Department of Defense v. Federal Labor Relations Authority
Department Of Revenue Of Oregon v. Acf Industries, Inc.
J.E.B. v. Alabama ex rel T.B.
description: Question: Was the use of peremptory challenges to exclude jurors solely because of their gender a violation of the equal protection clause of the Fourteenth Amendment?

name: Harris v. Forklift Systems, Inc.
description: Question: Must sexual harassment "seriously affect [an employee's] psychological well being" in order to create an "abusive work environment" that violates Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964?

name: Albright v. Oliver
description: Question: Can a citizen prosecuted without probable cause obtain relief under 42 U.S.C. 1983 for the deprivation of substantive due process rights?

name: Izumi Seimitsu Kogyo Kabushiki Kaisha v. U. S. Philips Corp.
John Hancock Mut. Life Ins. Company v. Harris Trust & Savings Bank
Florence County School District Four v. Carter
description: Question: May a court order reimbursement for parents who withdrew their child from a public school providing an inappropriate education under the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act and put the child in a private school that is in substantial - but not complete - compliance with the act?

name: United States v. James Daniel Good Real Property
Posters 'N' Things, Ltd. v. United States
Thunder Basin Coal Company v. Reich
Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation v. Meyer
Johnson v. Texas
description: Question: Did the Texas capital sentencing statute unconstitutionally preclude the jury from fully considering the mitigating effect of the petitioner's youth at the time of the crime?

name: Godinez v. Moran
description: Question: Does the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment require a trial court to apply a heightened "reasoned choice" standard to determine the competency of a defendant to enter a plea of guilty or waive counsel?

name: United States v. Edge Broadcasting Company
Wisconsin v. Mitchell
description: Question: Did the increase in Mitchell's sentence based on his bigoted motives violate his First Amendment rights?

name: Shaw v. Reno
description: A case in which the Court held that the redistricting of North Carolina was evidence of an attempt to separate voters based on race, and thus raised a constitutional issue under the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.

name: St. Mary's Honor Center v. Hicks
Austin v. United States
description: A case in which the Court held that the Excessive Fines Clause of the Eighth Amendment applied to a statutory in rem forfeiture of property.

name: United States National Bank of Oregon v. Independent Insurance Agents of America, Inc.
TXO Production Corporation v. Alliance Resources Corporation
Daubert v. Merrell Dow Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
Federal Communications Commission v. Beach Communications, Inc.
description: Question: Is there a conceivable rational basis justifying the distinction between cable facilities that serve separately owned and managed buildings and those that serve one or more buildings under common ownership or management for purposes of the Due Process Clause of the Fifth Amendment?

name: Brooke Group Ltd. v. Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corporation
United States v. Idaho ex rel. Director, Idaho Dept. of Water Resources
Smith v. United States
description: Question: Does trading a gun for drugs make a convicted defendant eligible for sentence enhancement under a federal law, which requires such treatment if the defendant "during and in relation to . . . [a] drug trafficking crime[,] uses . . . a firearm?"

name: Oklahoma Tax Commission v. Sac and Fox Nation
Heller  v. Doe
description: Question: Do Kentucky's involuntary commitment procedures for retarded persons violate the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment?

name: Minnesota v. Dickerson
description: Question: When a police officer detects contraband through his or her sense of touch during a protective patdown search, does the Fourth Amendment permit its seizure and subsequent introduction into evidence? Was the police officer who frisked Dickerson adhering to the Fourth Amendment when he formed the belief, through his sense of touch, that the lump in Dickerson's jacket pocket was cocaine?

name: Cardinal Chemical Company v. Morton International, Inc.
description: Question: Can a federal court, with exclusive jurisdiction over all federal appeals concerning patent litigation, use its finding that a patent has not been infringed as a per se justification for upholding the validity of the disputed patents themselves?

name: Sale v. Haitian Centers Council, Inc.
description: Question: Is Executive Order No. 12807 a violation of section 243(h) or Article 33?

name: Deal v. United States
description: Question: Does a criminal's second through sixth convictions under section 924(c)(1) in a single proceeding arise "in the case of his second or subsequent conviction" within the meaning of section 924(c)(1)?

name: Moreau v. Klevenhagen
description: Question: Can the Sheriff’s department take advantage of the compensatory time exception from the FLSA absent a collective bargaining agreement in a state that prohibits collective bargaining agreements, but employees have a union representative for other purposes?

name: Musick, Peeler & Garrett v. Employers Insurance of Wausau
Zobrest v. Catalina Foothills School District
description: Question: May a school district decline to provide an interpreter to a deaf child based on the Establishment Clause of the First Amendment?

name: Lamb's Chapel v. Center Moriches Union Free School District
description: Question: Did the District violate the First Amendment's freedom of speech when it denied Lamb's Chapel the use of school premises to show religious-oriented films?

name: Hartford Fire Insurance Company v. California
description: Question: First, did the plaintiffs sufficiently allege "boycotts," as used in the McCarran-Ferguson Act, Section 3(b)? Second, did international comity counsel against exercising Sherman Act jurisdiction over the conduct of the London-based defendants?

name: United States v. California
description: Question: May the United States Government receive compensation for the state of California's allegedly unfounded taxation of a private federal contractor?

name: Granite State Insurance Company v. Tandy Corporation
Northeastern Florida Chapter, Associated General Contractors of America v. City of Jacksonville, Florida
description: Question: In order to have standing to challenge the Jacksonville, Florida ordinance favoring minority-owned businesses, must an association of contractors demonstrate that at least one of its members would have received a city contract in the absence of the ordinance?

name: Commissioner v. Keystone Consol. Industries, Inc.
Hazen Paper Company v. Biggins
description:
Question: Did the Courts below err in sustaining Biggin's claim under the ADEA, where the finding of age discrimination was based on pension vesting?
Did the Court of Appeals err in reinstating an award of liquidated damages for willful ADEA violation that had been set aside by the District Court?

name: Helling v. McKinney
description: Question: May an inmate sue to prove that his Eighth Amendment right to be free from cruel and unusual punishment has been violated by prison officials who act with "deliberate indifference" to the future health risks associated with second-hand smoke?

name: Leatherman v. Tarrant County Narcotics Intelligence and Coordination Unit
Alexander v. United States
description:
Question:
